## Mapping and routed evaluation

Unmodified `make fpga TARGET=bench`, with NRET=1 and the existing single-issue FPGA wrapper, completed all three seeds. All build products were staged under TMPDIR. Yosys 0.64+149 / nextpnr 0.10-45-g98c18d7f were used.

Mapped netlist traversal confirms separate 32-flop integer, multiply and divider banks. The DSP lies in the multiply bank's combinational capture cone and is absent from the integer bank's capture cone. MEM/WB's ALU-data cone ends at exactly the 96 registered data bits plus the two registered class bits, with no live-opcode or completion-data boundary. Forwarding and MEM/WB share the selected source. The intermediate selected wire name is optimized into consumers; disconnected netname aliases were not treated as proof of separation. The direct normal address bank remains separate.

Resources: **one MULT36X36, four DPX9B block RAMs, 5,515 routed LUT4 equivalents, 2,124 FF**. The recorded starting resources are 5,490 LUT4 / 2,112 FF. Thus the complete mapped design grows by 25 LUT4 equivalents and 12 FF after optimization, despite the source-level addition of 33 register bits. No product registers per multiply operation or multiplier replication were introduced.

| Seed | Final routed MHz | Reported worst path | Logic / routing |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | 175.25 | Register file x15 bit 11 through read mux to ID/EX operand capture | 2.76 / 2.95 ns |
| 2 | 171.67 | EX/MEM destination metadata through forwarding selection and JALR target arithmetic to PC | 3.06 / 2.77 ns |
| 3 | 167.56 | EX/MEM destination metadata through forwarding selection and JALR target arithmetic to PC | 3.04 / 2.93 ns |

Evaluator fitness is **382.21** using 10 / 4,491,485 iterations/cycle, median 171.67 MHz. Recomputing the recorded starting frequency at those identical cycles gives 409.80. The evaluator's displayed `ipc_coremark=2e-06` is rounded; it is not used to recompute fitness here. Applying the same median to the supplemental stalled 6 KB run gives 52.28 iterations/second, separately labeled and not substituted into the evaluator result.

## Timing coverage limitation

**The existing result-bank timing coverage gap continues in all three seeds.** Separate diagnostic runs with SDF/detailed reports reproduced the official routed JSON designs exactly, including identical placement, routing and Fmax. No timing model or constraint was changed.

All three SDFs contain 37 LUT3 cells under `cpu.u_ex.div_result_sel_q_MUX2_LUT5_S0*` with **no IOPATH entries**. Concrete multiply-bank-to-EX and multiply-bank-to-WB connectivity crosses those cells. For example:

- Multiply Q (`mul_result_q_DFFR_Q_15`) to normal EX result D (`reg_q_DFFR_Q_78`) crosses `div_result_sel_q_MUX2_LUT5_S0_4_I0_LUT3_F.I1->F`, which has no timing arc, followed by forwarding/ALU logic with further missing LUT arcs.
- Multiply Q (`mul_result_q_DFFR_Q`) to MEM/WB ALU D (`u_mem.reg_q_DFFR_Q_67`) crosses `div_result_sel_q_MUX2_LUT5_S0_9_I0_LUT3_F.I1->F`, also absent, and an unmodeled packing passthrough LUT.

Integer and divider bank paths to the same consumer classes also cross missing arcs. These are topology witnesses, not worst-path delay estimates. **Complete bank-to-EX and bank-to-WB delays are unavailable, not zero.** The reported Fmax/fitness regression is the unchanged evaluator's result under this incomplete timing coverage; it does not establish complete physical timing or any frequency gain from separating the bank.

Attempting to re-import saved P&R JSON for timing export alone hit nextpnr's `array2d.h:78` assertion on all seeds. The subsequent diagnostic reroutes resolved report generation and exactly reproduced the successful official routes; they were not additional fitness samples.

## Evidence and deviations

Evidence directory: `/Users/bonetto/bonetto/auto-arch-tournament/.claude/astra-max-20260905/bench-runs/gpt-6-astra_max-rep2/.tmp/r7s1-multiply-banks/`.

It contains the immutable starting RTL, validated candidate snapshot, `formal_gate.log`, unit/pipeline/reset logs, `pipeline_traces/`, `selftest_cosim.json`, `coremark_comparison.json`, both ELF binaries, `mapped_separation.json`, `fpga_result.json`, the official three routed seeds, `routed_bank_timing_coverage.json`, and diagnostic per-seed SDF/timing JSON. Final RTL was byte-compared with the validated candidate snapshot.

No architectural deviation from the hypothesis. Validation used private scratch copies because the formal runner writes into its framework directory and the benchmark Makefile creates ELF files. The explicitly requested notes file is at the worktree root, which the orchestrator reads and permits. No tracked contract/evaluator/other-core file was changed. Remaining concerns are the measured fitness regression and incomplete timing arcs, not a known functional failure.
lesson: - 2026-09-06 hyp-20260906-002-r7s1 (regression, -6.73%): Separating MUL into an EX/MEM bank left EX/MEM rd-to-JALR forwarding and register-file reads limiting reported Fmax despite unchanged CoreMark cycles and one MULT36X36; missing result-bank mux arcs prevent attributing the regression to bank-to-EX/WB delay.

title: Single-entry backedge target prediction with decode validation
motivation:
The current core fetches sequentially and loses one fetch/decode slot on
an advancing taken branch because IF/ID is combinational. Prior predictor
experiments establish useful cycle savings but very little timing budget:
r2s2's 16-entry BTB saved 6.135% of cycles but lost 13.074% median Fmax,
with EX qualification driving wide predictor write enables; r5s2's static
backward predictor saved 4.05% of cycles but lost 14.98% median Fmax.
Removing state or narrowing squash fanout alone did not solve timing.
r6s2 moved validation to MEM and failed the unchanged liveness check,
so its longer recovery must not be assumed viable.

Try a much smaller learned predictor for repeated loop backedges. A
single resident branch removes the indexed table read and broad write
fanout. A cached displacement lets decode certify the target without
putting instruction predecode or a new target adder in fetch, or a
full actual-versus-predicted PC comparison in EX. This is a new timing
tradeoff, not evidence that a smaller predictor necessarily routes faster.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fully tagged last-taken-backedge target entry. It contains valid,
source PC[31:2], target[31:2], and the exact B displacement bits [12:1]:
73 logical state bits before constant-bit optimization. A lookup hit
requires valid, word-aligned fetch PC, and equality of all source-PC
bits [31:2]. On a hit predict the stored full-width aligned target;
otherwise predict full-width PC+4. Use no direction counter, indexed
array, return stack, or separate jump predictor. Only an accepted legal,
taken conditional branch with negative displacement, aligned source PC,
and aligned target can replace the entry. Not-taken branches, forward
branches, and jumps leave it unchanged. It therefore retains a hot
inner-loop backedge across intervening non-backedge control transfers.
Nested backedges can evict one another; cold starts and loop exits cost
ordinary EX repairs. No address-range truncation or workload PC constants
are permitted. Addition remains modulo 2^32, including page crossings.

Lookup and target selection depend only on registered PC and entry
contents. Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC register. Select the
raw lookup result in the PC data mux, and apply it only on actual fetch
acceptance into ID/EX; do not put acceptance, flush, or div_wait in the
prediction-select data cone. Reset and existing EX repair retain priority
over prediction. Hold fetch on ordinary load-use, bus, and divider stalls.
A prediction never squashes the instruction that produced it.

Carry prediction_used and the cached displacement snapshot with the
accepting IF/ID instruction. Simultaneous lookup/update consumes the
pre-edge entry, with no update bypass. In ID, certify a predicted target
only if the CURRENT instruction decodes as a legal conditional branch
and its complete B displacement equals the saved displacement. The
source-PC tag already matched the exact accepted PC, and training wrote
source, target, and displacement coherently, so this equality proves the
predicted target equals this instruction's architectural branch target.
It needs only immediate-bit comparison, not another PC-relative adder.
Changes in branch condition or source registers do not invalidate that
proof; EX must evaluate the current condition using forwarded operands.
Register prediction_used, certified_backedge, and the repair polarity
with ID/EX. Keep the architectural branch_op unchanged. For a certified
prediction, fold inversion of the outcome into the registered branch
repair polarity, as in the earlier decode-folded comparator design.

Keep recovery in EX and specify all three cases explicitly:
(1) No consumed prediction: retain the existing branch/jump redirect
and target-alignment behavior.
(2) Certified backedge: redirect only when its condition is false, to
PC+4; a taken outcome has no flush or bubble.
(3) Consumed but uncertified prediction: force repair to the current
instruction's actual architectural next PC, for EVERY instruction class.
That includes changed branch displacements, JAL/JALR, ordinary ALU,
load/store, DIV/REM, illegal encodings, and alignment traps. Use the
existing PC+4 trap continuation and suppress trapped jump link writes.
This conservative stale-entry repair needs no full predicted-PC field
or full-PC mismatch comparator in EX. A stale branch's actual outcome
still selects target versus fall-through correctly; stale jumps use
the current forwarded target. Keep this exceptional target selection
separate from the common certified-exit PC+4 and ordinary redirect paths.

Qualify repair with valid and reset, retaining the existing level-style
EX repair behavior through holds. A held owner may repeatedly request
the same repair; it must retain its operands and prediction flags until
advancement. Do not add a generic EX-accept/div_wait gate to the common
branch repair cone. In particular, an uncertified prediction on DIV/REM
must not flush that owner or cancel its divide: existing divider-hold
priority retains ID/EX until completion, then the repair clears the
younger slot on the accepting edge. Memory holds similarly defer owner
advancement. Repairs override unavailable imem. Flush only the younger
combinational fetch/decode slot, preserving the current recovery depth.

Stage predictor writes independently of recovery. Register a one-cycle
train_pending pulse when the qualifying backward branch actually enters
EX/MEM, using valid, legality, alignment, taken outcome, and !stall.
Clear that pulse on every other clock, including holds and bubbles.
On the following edge the predictor writes the coherent source, target,
and displacement from the existing EX/MEM pc, branch_target, and instr
payload. Those fields were captured on the same edge as train_pending;
nonblocking update semantics preserve their association on the write
edge. Reuse these payload fields instead of adding another wide training
bank. Only registered train_pending enables entry writes, with no live
EX comparator, resident-entry match, or memory-ready signal in that
write-enable cone. Each accepted branch trains once even when subsequent
pipeline work stalls. Reset cancels pending training and clears entry
validity; inactive uninitialized entry payload cannot affect a miss.

Preserve the winner's independent pipeline payload capture and narrow
control/valid squashes. Hold accepted prediction metadata with its owner;
invalid entries have inert repair/training controls. Preserve the decoder,
arithmetic, divider completion bank, retained WB forwarding data, direct
registered dmem address, actual RVFI pc_next, and nret=1 external ports.
This experiment changes only backedge prediction and its integration.

Estimate 2% higher fitness with low confidence. The explicit working
assumption is 2.5% fewer marker-window cycles with at most 0.5% median
Fmax loss, yielding about 2.05% net gain. This is a forecast, not a
measurement; the one-entry coverage may be too small. Against 184.06 MHz
and 409.80 iter/sec, a 2.5% cycle reduction breaks even near 179.46 MHz.
Count useful hits, loop-exit/stale repairs, and backedge replacements
inside the existing timing markers. Run unchanged lint, unit, formal
including liveness, cosim, CRC/UART, OOB, marker, resource, and three-seed
FPGA gates. Inspect all routed seeds for lookup-to-PC, repair-to-squash,
and training-enable timing, including unchanged paths displaced by
routing. Keep evaluator fitness authoritative and any separately built
6 KB measurement distinct, as prior notes document a fixture discrepancy.
Do not change any evaluator, formal bound, other core, or hard invariant.

Implemented the single-entry backedge predictor as specified. Correctness gates pass, but the measured timing loss rejects the forecasted fitness gain: the unchanged local evaluator reports 115.85 MHz median and 268.66 iter/sec, versus the supplied winner's 184.06 MHz and 409.80 iter/sec. These are approximately 37.06% lower Fmax and 34.44% lower fitness. No acceptance decision or evaluator record was changed.

The RTL changes are confined to cores/bench/rtl:

- Added branch_predictor.sv with one valid bit, 30 source bits, 30 target bits, and the complete 12-bit B displacement. Synthesis retains all 73 entry flops. Only validity resets; reset cancels a pending payload write. Miss outputs are zero. Lookup requires exact source equality and word alignment, uses full addresses, and has no update bypass.
- IF selects the raw lookup target versus full-width PC+4. Reset and existing EX repair have priority; normal advancement requires fetch acceptance. imem_addr still comes directly from the PC register. A prediction does not flush its own instruction.
- IF/ID carries the lookup-use bit and displacement snapshot. ID compares every B displacement bit against a current legal branch decode, preserving architectural branch_op and source-register fields. ID/EX carries prediction_used, certified_backedge, and branch_op[0] XOR certified_backedge as registered repair polarity. Invalid/flush controls are inert, holds retain all owner metadata, and independent payload capture remains intact.
- EX shares equality/signed-less-than/unsigned-less-than predicates between actual branch resolution and the decode-folded repair polarity. No prediction uses ordinary EX recovery; certified predictions repair only false outcomes to PC+4; stale predictions always repair to the current architectural next PC, including illegal encodings, alignment traps, memory operations, and DIV/REM. The exceptional actual-next-PC selection remains separate from the ordinary redirect and certified-exit selections. RVFI always carries the actual next PC.
- EX repair is qualified by valid and reset, with no new EX-accept/div_wait gate. The unchanged hazard priority retains held memory/divider owners and clears only the younger combinational slot when the owner advances. Trapped jumps still suppress link writes.
- A registered train_pending pulse is generated only for an accepted legal aligned taken negative-displacement conditional branch. It clears on every other clock, including holds. The following edge writes the existing EX/MEM pc, branch_target and instruction displacement. There is no additional training payload bank, resident-state feedback, or live EX/memory-ready write enable.

No architectural deviations were needed. The decoder, arithmetic/divider implementation, divider completion bank, retained WB forwarding, hazard priority, directly registered dmem address, and nret=1 external port set are unchanged. Test-only additions include dynamic instruction versions and optional marker-window counters; there are no hardware event counters, workload PC constants, address truncations, new prediction classes, or evaluator/formal-bound changes.

title: Infer distributed register storage by resetting per-register validity
motivation:
reg_file.sv synchronously clears every word of its 32-by-32 data array.
That whole-array reset prevents mapping the storage to the installed
Gowin LUT RAM primitive, whose interface has a synchronous write port,
an asynchronous read port, and no bulk-clear input. The current design
therefore retains a large resettable register bank and read-selection
network. The recorded 409.80 winner's seed-2 limiting path passes through
register-file reads into ID/EX; seeds 1 and 3 instead limit on forwarding
and JALR, so a frequency improvement is plausible but not assured.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt records were reviewed. In particular,
hyp-20260906-001-r5s0 changed the read/bypass tree while explicitly keeping
resettable storage, and lost 7.44% median Fmax. This proposal changes the
storage inference pattern itself. It does not repeat that one-hot read
tree, the failed ALU recoding, or the divider arithmetic rewrites.

hyp-20260906-001-r5s0 changed the read/bypass tree while explicitly keeping

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace physical clearing of register data with one synchronously reset
written-since-reset bit per architectural register. Preserve the existing
reg_file interface, two combinational reads, one synchronous write, and
every externally observable reset and write-first behavior. This is a
local storage implementation optimization with no added pipeline stage,
read latency, instruction scheduling change, or memory-hierarchy change.

Keep a normally indexed 32-by-32 data array with
(* ram_style = "distributed" *). Its only clocked assignment is a write
to data[w_addr] when !reset && w_en && w_addr != 0. Do not put a reset
assignment, initialization loop, or per-word read expansion on this data
array. In a separate clocked process, reset a 32-bit written_q vector to
zero; otherwise set written_q[w_addr] on exactly the same accepted write.
Leave all other validity bits unchanged, and keep bit zero clear.

Each read retains this exact priority: address zero returns zero; an
enabled same-address write returns live w_data; otherwise an unset
written_q bit returns zero; otherwise return the indexed stored word.
The combinational write-hit predicate remains independent of reset,
matching the starting RTL even when reset and w_en overlap. Reset wins
at the edge, clears validity, and suppresses the storage write. Once the
bypass is removed after that edge, every unwritten register reads zero.
Thus stale or uninitialized physical RAM contents never become visible,
including through the core's raw-source RVFI metadata.

The installed gowin/lutrams.txt and lutrams_map.v support this synchronous
write/asynchronous read pattern using RAM16SDP primitives. Let ordinary
Yosys memory mapping replicate read storage and bank the 32-word depth;
use behavioral RTL shared by synthesis, simulation, and formal. The
expected mapping is roughly two read replicas totaling 32 RAM16SDP4
cells, replacing most of the 31-by-32 resettable data flops and their
flop-based read multiplexers. Exact cell counts are a validation result,
not an assumption. The documented inference attribute is described in
[Yosys memory mapping](https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/latest/using_yosys/synthesis/memory.html#memory-kind-selection).

The proposed fitness gain comes entirely from higher routed Fmax through
more compact register storage, simpler data reads, and reduced reset and
write-data fanout. Instruction and memory-handshake timing should remain
identical. The added validity selection, distributed-RAM placement
restrictions, and unchanged competing EX paths could erase the benefit;
the five-percent estimate is unmeasured.

Validate the storage mapping in the unchanged full-core synth_gowin flow:
identify the register-file RAM cells, quantify the data-FF reduction,
and inspect both read-address/data and validity/bypass timing paths in
all three routed seeds. Preserve the four existing wrapper block RAMs,
shared multiplier, direct registered dmem address, and divider banks.
An area reduction alone does not confirm the hypothesis. Run the existing
unit, formal, and cosim gates, then compare starting/candidate retirement
timing and marker-window cycles with identical ELF bytes and bus-stall
schedules. Use the unchanged median-of-three FPGA evaluator for fitness;
retain canonical 6 KB CRC, UART, bounded-access, and marker validation.
If the logged evaluator-versus-6-KB workload discrepancy persists, report
the two measurements separately without modifying any evaluation file.

implementation_notes:
# Distributed register storage with reset validity

Implemented the proposed storage pattern without changing instruction or bus timing. Correctness gates pass, but the measured hypothesis regresses fitness: median routed Fmax falls from 184.06 to 160.15 MHz (-12.99%), and the unchanged evaluator reports 409.80 -> 356.56 iterations/second. The implementation is retained for the orchestrator to evaluate; the predicted frequency improvement is not confirmed.

## Implementation and scope

- `cores/bench/rtl/reg_file.sv`: a binary-indexed `(* ram_style = "distributed" *)` 32-by-32 `data` array receives only the accepted synchronous write (`!reset && w_en && w_addr != 0`). It has no reset, initialization, or expanded per-word reads. A separate synchronous process resets `written_q`, sets only the accepted destination, and keeps bit zero clear. Read priority is exactly x0, live same-address write, unwritten zero, stored data. The live bypass remains independent of reset.
- `cores/bench/test/test_reg_file.py`: retained all five existing tests and added an independent public-port architectural scoreboard. It checks all 32 destinations, all 1,024 read-address pairs repeatedly, both and single port collisions, first writes, overwrites, disabled writes, and randomized changes without clock edges. Each of 32 reset/write destination cases follows a fully populated distinct nonzero bank; bypass is checked before and after reset edges, then every read pair is checked with bypass removed. Repeated reset edges and 512 randomized clock intervals are included.
- `cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py`: retained the ISS, operand, order, PC, memory-acceptance, divider, payload and stall assertions. The new test populates all nonzero registers, resets the same DUT, checks all raw source registers through ADD and ADDI instructions writing x0, and exercises first-write WB-to-ID collisions on each read port and both together. Dependent ALU/load/store/divide consumers run with deterministic instruction/data holds. Two different populated histories must produce identical full RVFI, memory effects, and all 89 retirement cycles. The cycle sequence was measured with starting RTL commit `7583066de166bd6cd773a698ecfc285232a61ed3` and is asserted in the test.

Only the register-file RTL and these two tests changed. The checkout declares `nret: 1`; the existing single-channel core interface and wrapper selection were preserved. The writeup is at the explicitly requested worktree-root location, which the orchestrator reads. No evaluation source or other core was changed.

## Local correctness validation

- Requested `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP -sv +incdir+cores/bench/rtl cores/bench/rtl/*.sv`: PASS, no warnings. `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Unit suite: nine pytest runners, 142 cocotb tests, all PASS. The starting RTL also passed the expanded register-file and pipeline suites. After adding the measured baseline cycle assertion, the final candidate pipeline suite was rerun: 23/23 PASS.
- Local formal: **PASS on the first invocation, 53 passed / 0 failed; zero fix attempts.** Ran the unchanged `bash formal/run_all.sh` with `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=4`, auto-selecting `wrapper_si.sv` and `checks_si.cfg`. This is the existing ALTOPS gate. No counterexample occurred. Real arithmetic remains covered by the existing unit/cosim gates; formal-deep was not needed for this register-file-only change.
- Unchanged `tools.eval.cosim.run_cosim`: PASS, both selftest and evaluator CoreMark ELFs. The selftest uses the unchanged ISS comparison; CoreMark uses the unchanged UART/CRC validation.

Tests, formal staging, compilation, ELF generation and FPGA outputs used private copies under `$TMPDIR`, avoiding writes to the shared formal submodule or protected worktree paths. Staged contract files were compared byte-for-byte against the worktree (193 files plus the formal scripts/configs). Final candidate RTL and test copies match the edited worktree. Available conda Python supplied pytest/cocotb; the RTL was not adapted to the environment.

## Full-core mapping and routed timing

Both versions used unchanged `fpga/scripts/synth.tcl` / `synth_gowin`, `core_bench_si.sv`, constraints, seeds 1/2/3, and the unchanged median-of-three evaluator. The starting run reproduces the recorded 409.80 winner.

| Measurement | Starting | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Register-file RAM16SDP4 cells | 0 | 32 |
| Register-file data DFFE cells | 1,014 | 0 |
| Register-file validity FF cells | 0 | 32 |
| Total synthesized FF cells | 2,112 | 1,127 |
| Evaluator routed LUT4 resources | 5,490 | 3,155 |
| Evaluator routed DFF resources | 2,112 | 1,319 |
| Wrapper DPX9B cells (packed as DP) | 4 | 4 |
| Shared MULT36X36 cells | 1 | 1 |
| Divider FF cells | 169 | 169 |

The inferred RAMs are `cpu.u_rf.data.0.0` through `.0.15` and `.1.0` through `.1.15`: two read replicas, each banked to 32 words. The starting data FF count includes 992 cells for x1..x31 and 22 retained cells named for x0. Candidate validity uses 31 DFFRE plus one DFFR. The total synthesized FF reduction is 985; the routed resource counter is a different measurement and is reported separately. The direct normal-result dmem address and both divider/result banks remain unchanged, and all four wrapper block RAMs still map successfully.

| Routed seed | Starting MHz | Candidate MHz | Candidate limiting path |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 184.06 | 160.15 | ID/EX source-address metadata -> forwarding selection -> JALR/PC, 6.24 ns (2.96 logic + 3.28 routing) |
| 2 | 191.13 | 161.52 | written_q[2] -> read selection -> ID/EX rs2_val[22], 6.19 ns (2.88 logic + 3.31 routing) |
| 3 | 179.89 | 158.40 | written_q[21] -> read selection -> ID/EX rs2_val[31], 6.31 ns (2.93 logic + 3.38 routing) |
| Median | 184.06 | 160.15 | -12.99% |

Starting seeds 1 and 3 limit on EX/MEM destination forwarding into JALR/PC; seed 2 limits on the LFSR instruction/read-address path through the register-file read into ID/EX. Candidate seed 1 has synthesized cell names containing `written_q` on shared logic, but its launch register is ID/EX metadata, not a validity bit.

Additional diagnostic runs appended only JSON timing/SDF output options and reproduced all six evaluator frequencies exactly. Inspection covered both RAM read replicas, read-address routing, data reads, validity, and WB-to-ID selection for every routed seed:

| Observed diagnostic quantity, ns | Seed 1 | Seed 2 | Seed 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Longest route into a RAM RAD pin (128 routes per seed) | 1.717 | 1.451 | 2.150 |
| RAM clock-to-word through available arcs to ID rs1 / rs2 | 2.769 / 2.508 | 2.578 / 2.815 | 2.765 / 2.627 |
| Validity through available arcs to ID rs2 | 5.970 | 6.191 | 6.313 |
| WB selection through available arcs to ID rs1 / rs2 | 4.787 / 3.848 | 4.636 / 4.791 | 4.898 / 4.435 |

The installed SDF exposes RAM RAD-to-DO arcs (0.370..0.569 ns maximum delay by input pin), but omits IOPATH arcs for some surrounding LUT2/LUT3 cells, including `cpu.u_id.u_decoder.instr_LUT2_F_5`. Therefore the diagnostic path numbers are observations over exported arcs, not exhaustive timing bounds: complete read-address-to-ID and rs1-validity delays are not established by that export. No missing delay was invented and no diagnostic estimate replaced the evaluator Fmax. The reported critical validity paths in seeds 2/3 are fully present. Compact storage improves the available word-read paths, while validity selection and unchanged competing paths erase the proposed benefit.

The storage attribute/pattern agrees with the installed `gowin/lutrams.txt` and `lutrams_map.v`, and the documented [Yosys memory-kind selection](https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/latest/using_yosys/synthesis/memory.html#memory-kind-selection). No vendor primitive or separate formal implementation was introduced.

## Identical workloads and timing comparison

The evaluator-versus-6-KB discrepancy persists: the unchanged evaluator requires 2-KB CRCs and the unchanged benchmark Makefile defaults to 2,000 total bytes. Both measurements are kept separate. Each ELF was built from unchanged sources with `-O3`, RV32IM, and ITERATIONS=10; the 6-KB build uses the existing `COREMARK_SIZE=6000 COREMARK_OPT=-O3` options. The port's UART compiler-flags string still says `-O2`; actual build commands are retained in the scratch logs. That string was not changed.

For each workload, both versions consumed the exact same ELF bytes and the unchanged harness's identical default PRNG bus schedule with `--istall --dstall`. Every emitted retirement record, including its cycle, was compared byte-for-byte in a streaming comparison. Separate `--bench --istall --dstall` runs compared the complete final retirement and marker/UART records. Both versions reached EBREAK, remained in bounds, emitted `Correct operation validated.`, and supplied valid positive start/stop marker windows.

| Measurement | Evaluator 2 KB | Canonical 6 KB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Identical retirement records | 2,937,037 | 22,093,920 |
| Last retirement cycle | 4,514,348 | 32,900,232 |
| Start marker cycle | 15,801 | 56,393 |
| Stop marker cycle | 4,507,286 | 32,893,064 |
| Marker-window cycles, both versions | 4,491,485 | 32,836,671 |
| Starting iterations/s | 409.80 (evaluator) | 56.0532 (separate calculation) |
| Candidate iterations/s | 356.56 (evaluator) | 48.7717 (separate calculation) |

The 2-KB run passes the unchanged evaluator validator. The separate 6-KB run checks the required CRCs `crclist=0xd4b0`, `crcmatrix=0xbe52`, `crcstate=0x5e47`, ITERATIONS=10, literal UART validation, bounded accesses and both markers. title: Absorb ID operand capture into synchronous register-file RAM banks
motivation:
The structural entries in experiments/log.jsonl and LESSONS.md show that
changing storage boundaries can improve fitness without changing cycles:
r5s1 reached 409.80 at 184.06 MHz by separating payload capture from
pipeline control. Its reported seed-2 limit was instruction input through
register-file reading to ID operand capture; seeds 1 and 3 instead limited
on forwarding through JALR resolution. The r7s1 multiply-bank experiment
again exposed register-file reads and forwarding as competing limits.
These reports establish a real read-path target, not that it dominates
every seed of the current winner.

Today reg_file.sv resets the complete 32-by-32 array and performs two
asynchronous reads, followed by write-first bypass and ID/EX operand
flops. The r5s0 one-hot read-tree rewrite reduced area but regressed routed
timing; r6s1 forwarding-comparison retiming also regressed. No recorded
structural attempt moves register-file storage and operand capture into
synchronous RAM. This experiment removes the large fabric read network
by changing where operands are stored and clocked, while retaining the
current instruction schedule.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the asynchronous flop-based integer register file plus its two
ID/EX operand registers with two coherent inferred synchronous-read RAM
banks, one per source port. Broadcast the existing single WB write to
both banks. Each bank has independent read and write addresses and a
single shared clock. The RAM read edge must be the existing ID/EX capture
edge: instruction N's source addresses before that edge produce its
registered source values alongside instruction N's decoded metadata
after the edge. Do not add a fetch, operand-read, execute, or retirement
cycle. This is one structural change to register-file/ID storage ownership.

Infer block RAM using portable behavioral SystemVerilog and the RTL
ram_style attribute, with no vendor-only simulation replacement. Use
synchronous read outputs without bulk array reset. Preserve the existing
architectural reset-to-zero behavior with one resettable initialized-bit
bitmap shared by the two coherent copies. Every accepted nonzero WB
write sets its destination's bit; reset clears the bitmap and suppresses
writes. Capture each read's initialized/nonzero qualification on the
same edge as its RAM read. Unwritten registers and x0 return zero even
though raw RAM contents are unspecified. Reset also clears the captured
output qualifications so a held or previously populated output cannot
leak stale data after reset. Do not replace reset with a multi-cycle
memory-clearing sweep or expose unknown data to execution or RVFI.

Implement explicit same-edge write-first behavior for each read port.
Capture the nonzero WB address-match flag and the matching WB data with
the read transaction; select that registered data on a collision before
considering the captured initialized bit. A first write after reset must
therefore be visible to a simultaneous read. Neither later WB values,
live read addresses, nor later bitmap updates may change a held operand.
Do not depend on an unspecified primitive read/write collision result.
Keep raw memory/read-output storage free of reset muxes that would prevent
RAM inference; implement required reset visibility in the small response
qualification bank. The intended inference pattern is supported by the
Yosys memory documentation, but actual Gowin mapping must be inspected:
https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/v0.50/using_yosys/synthesis/memory.html

Drive both RAM read enables and all response metadata captures from the
same existing ID payload capture decision, !stall_id, with reset taking
priority in qualification state. WB writes remain independent of this
read enable, so older instructions can write while ID holds. A dmem or
divider hold retains both operand responses and all instruction metadata.
A load-use flush with stall retains payload while clearing control;
an unstalled redirect or invalid-fetch bubble follows the current
independent payload-capture policy. Assemble id_ex_t operands directly
from these registered responses; remove their redundant ID-stage capture
so the RAM result is never associated with the preceding instruction.
Keep ID metadata/control storage and the existing EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB
forwarding priority intact, including retained WB forwarding during
dmem stalls and captured DIV/REM operands during execution.

The expected benefit is fewer register-storage flops and fabric read
muxes, a shorter instruction-address-to-read-capture path, and potentially
less routing congestion. Target approximately two additional block RAMs,
but verify actual mapped geometry and device capacity. RAM clock-to-output
delay, registered collision selection, fixed RAM placement, and the
existing forwarding/JALR and ALU-control paths may erase the benefit.
The forecast is therefore a low-confidence 5% fitness gain with unchanged
marker-window cycles; it is not a measured improvement.

Keep core.yaml nret=1, the external core ports, decoder/trap rules,
retirement ordering, memory handshakes, direct EX/MEM memory-address
bank, divider latency/arithmetic, multiplier sharing, and all ALTOPS
formulas unchanged. Modify only the listed bench RTL and unit tests.
Run the existing lint, unit, formal, stalled ISS cosim, CoreMark CRC/UART,
bounds, marker, and three-seed FPGA gates without changing their contract.
Compare starting and candidate retirement cycles with identical programs
and stall sequences to verify that no read bubbles were introduced.
Verify the requested 6 KB CRCs and keep any separately reported fixture
measurements distinct without changing benchmark or evaluator files.
Inspect mapped RF RAMs, read-output absorption, collision forwarding,
reset masking, resources, and all three routed limiting paths. Check RAM
address and RAM-output-to-EX timing coverage; an omitted arc is not zero
delay. Accept only improvement in the unchanged evaluator's median-Fmax
times marker-bracketed iterations-per-cycle product.

implementation_notes:
The synchronous RAM register-file hypothesis is implemented, but **reject it as a fitness improvement**. The unchanged evaluator reports **385.46**, versus **409.80** for a fresh build and three-seed route of the starting RTL: **-5.94%**, with identical marker-window cycles. The implementation remains in the allowed bench RTL/tests for orchestrator review; it is not an accepted replacement for the starting winner.

`reg_file.sv` now contains two coherent 32-by-32 synchronous-read arrays with `ram_style="block"`. Both receive the same accepted nonzero WB write, independently of read enable. Reads, captured nonzero/initialized qualifications, collision flags, and a shared 32-bit collision-data register use the existing `!stall_id` capture decision. Collision data takes priority over initialized qualification, including a first write after reset. Reset suppresses writes and clears the shared initialized bitmap and four response qualification bits; RAM contents and raw read outputs have no reset. Held responses do not depend on subsequent addresses, writes, or bitmap updates.

`id_stage.sv` stores metadata/control in a local operand-free struct and assembles `id_ex_t` directly from that state and the RF's registered responses. There is no second operand capture. Metadata capture, control-zero bubbles, flush-plus-hold behavior, and invalid-fetch payload capture retain their existing policies. `core.sv` only adds the RF read-enable connection. Forwarding priority, retained MEM/WB forwarding during memory holds, saved DIV/REM operands, direct normal EX/MEM memory-address bank, arithmetic, multiplier sharing, ALTOPS, ports, and `core.yaml`/`nret: 1` are unchanged.

One mapping refinement beyond the advisory plan is `no_rw_check` on the two raw arrays. The initial inferred read-first memories caused Gowin mapping to insert delayed-write registers and additional transparency emulation, despite the explicit response bypass already hiding every raw collision. This attribute removes that redundant emulation; it does not relax the visible write-first contract. Simulators still use the same behavioral SystemVerilog, and the final formal gate also passes with raw collisions unspecified. This pattern is documented in [Yosys memory handling](https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/v0.50/using_yosys/synthesis/memory.html), under synchronous SDP with undefined collision behavior. A single collision-data register serves both ports because they can only collide with the same WB transaction.

The RF tests retain the original value assertions with edge-based sampling and add an independent architectural scoreboard, all 1,024 read-address pairs after initialization and reset, both-port and individual collisions, first writes, x0, populated-memory resets, suppressed reset-edge writes, changing addresses/WB while held, later initialization behind an unwritten held response, and 4,000 randomized transactions. The ID test drives RF responses after the metadata capture edge, so a redundant operand register would fail. Pipeline tests independently model WB/read capture, exercise producer distances and both operands, ALU/JALR/branch/store dependencies, load-use interlocks, DIV/REM, populated-register reset, imem stalls, long dmem holds, and older WB writes during ID holds. Existing ISS, control/payload retention, ordered retirement, and unique accepted-memory-effect assertions remain active.

- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=4 bash formal/run_all.sh`: **PASS, 53 passed, 0 failed** on the final implementation. Includes channel-0 liveness, unique, cover, illegal instructions, and register/PC checks. No formal counterexample or failed formal invocation; zero formal fix attempts. Earlier structural forms also passed. The unchanged single-retirement wrapper, depths, and ALTOPS configuration were used. Deep arithmetic formal was not run because arithmetic and divider latency were untouched.
- Starting and final RTL: **34 identical protocol scenarios, 6,093 complete RVFI records with exact retirement-cycle equality, and 1,515 identical accepted memory transactions**. The same deterministic random seeds and directed bus schedules were used. The integer prefix retires on consecutive cycles through WB/read collisions.
- Unchanged `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1`: **PASS**, selftest ISS and evaluator CoreMark CRC/UART gates.
- Additional C++ selftest runs with `--istall --dstall --seed 1/19/99`: **PASS**, 115 retirements each, field-for-field ISS agreement and byte-identical starting/final full RVFI traces including cycle numbers.
- Unchanged `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1 BENCH=fpga/core_bench_si.sv`: all three seeds route successfully, CoreMark completes, bounds/CRC/UART/marker checks pass. **The fitness improvement criterion fails.**

Mapping inspection confirms exactly two `SDPX9B` RF cells, each configured for 36-bit reads and writes: a 512-by-36 physical geometry using 32 addresses and 32 payload bits. Both RF clocks are identical, read CE matches the collision-data capture CE, write address/data/enable are broadcast coherently, and both primitive reset inputs are tied low. All 64 raw RF response bits are driven directly by RAM outputs, with no fabric operand-output flops. The shared bitmap maps to 31 resettable flops (x0 constant), qualification/collision state to four resettable flops, and collision data to 32 enabled flops. The final memory-libmap output has no extra read-first/transparency emulation cells. Area fell 48.56% in LUT4 and 47.68% in DFF, but this did not improve the median routed throughput.

All three final routed limiting paths were inspected. Separate runs adding only SDF/detailed report outputs reproduced each gate Fmax exactly; scoring still uses the unchanged gate.

| 3 | ID ALU operation bit 3 → ALU result selection → EX/MEM normal result bit 0 | 5.260 | 2.886 | 2.374 |

The physical RAM clock-to-output model therefore does not establish complete RAM-output-to-EX timing. Missing arcs are **unknown, not zero delay**; no complete address or operand-path timing claim is made, and no timing library, constraint, or evaluator was changed. title: Backward-branch prediction with validity-only EX annul
motivation:
The current core predicts sequentially and loses one useful fetch/decode
slot for each normally advancing taken control transfer. The branch-only
static predictor in r5s2 reduced evaluator cycles by 4.05%, but its repair
and hazard paths still reached the RESET pins of 24 ID/EX control, valid,
and prediction flops. Its median Fmax fell to 146.05 MHz. The single-entry
predictor in r7s2 similarly left forwarding/JALR alignment through repair
to ID control RESET critical and regressed fitness by 34.44%. Registered
training did not solve this recovery bottleneck. Moving recovery to MEM
in r6s2 failed the unchanged liveness check. These results favor retaining
EX recovery while reducing its ID/EX destination to one validity bit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one static backward-taken conditional-branch predictor whose
EX recovery annuls the younger slot solely through its registered valid
bit. The new architectural claim is that validity-qualified consumers
can make the previously measured branch-cycle saving profitable by
removing repair from the entire ID/EX decode-control bank as well as
its data payload. Retain the existing pipeline depth and one-slot EX
repair penalty. Use the branch-only policy from r5s2 to isolate this
change in predictor recovery; JAL/JALR remain sequentially predicted.

IF predecodes raw imem_data for opcode 0x63 and legal funct3 values
0, 1, 4, 5, 6, and 7. Predict taken only for a negative B displacement
(instruction bit 31), word-aligned fetch PC, and instruction bit 8 clear.
Construct the sign-extended B displacement and add it to the full PC;
preserve all 32 address bits and modulo-2^32 carry behavior. Compute
PC+4 independently. Select between these values using raw eligibility,
independent of stall, flush, redirect, and acceptance qualification.
Update the PC only on the existing accepted fetch edge, with reset and
EX repair taking priority. Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC
register. There is no table, training, saved target, or additional stage.

Carry predicted_taken with the exact raw instruction used to choose
the fetch next PC. IF always exposes raw instruction and prediction
bits; flush and instruction unavailability affect validity only.
Remove the redirect-driven NOP mux so repair cannot reach the decoded
control D inputs through instruction masking. In ID, keep architectural
branch_op unchanged and register repair_invert = branch_op[0] XOR
predicted_taken. Register branch_repair_enable for a decoded legal
branch with an aligned target, using only the two-bit sum of PC and
immediate low bits. These three metadata bits use ordinary payload
capture and hold rules and are meaningful only when ID/EX is valid.

Make ID/EX valid the sole dynamically squashed ID/EX field. Its existing
reset, flush, and stall priority remains: an eligible flush clears valid,
an ordinary capture takes fetch validity, and a memory/divider hold
retains the current owner. The complete ctrl_t, prediction metadata,
and existing instruction/data fields have synchronous reset and the
ordinary !stall capture enable only. Capture raw decoded controls on
an advancing edge even when fetch is invalid or a repair discards it.
A load-use flush clears valid while its ordinary stall retains payload.
Do not zero or mask the control bank with flush or fetch validity, and
do not mask the ID/EX output bundle with valid. Invalid raw controls
are intentionally unspecified as instructions but remain defined bits.

Qualify every action that can consume these raw ID/EX controls with
the registered owner validity. Specifically, pass ID/EX valid into
hazard_unit and compute load_use_hazard from valid AND mem_read before
comparing rd with the raw fetched register addresses. Do not gate this
comparison with repair-dependent fetch validity or masked instructions;
the current valid branch/jump cannot simultaneously be an EX load.
Keep EX redirect and divider request/wait/accept qualified by in.valid;
audit that no invalid opcode can stall, redirect, or launch arithmetic.
Preserve EX/MEM's existing control-zero bubble conversion whenever
!in.valid or div_wait. Thus downstream forwarding producers and memory
requests still see zero controls for invalid EX/MEM entries. Preserve
retained MEM/WB forwarding data during dmem holds, including valid=0
retention after retirement; do not add a MEM/WB-valid forwarding gate.

EX shares forwarded equality, signed-less-than, and unsigned-less-than
predicates. Select base_cond with architectural branch_op[2:1]; use
original branch_op[0] for architectural direction and the registered
repair_invert for direction mismatch. Branch repair is in.valid AND
branch_repair_enable AND (base_cond XOR repair_invert). Combine it with
the current valid, legal, aligned JAL/JALR redirect contribution.
A predicted branch exit repairs to PC+4; an unpredicted taken branch
repairs to its branch target. Select the branch repair target from
registered predicted_taken, independently of the live comparison.
Correct predictions preserve the useful younger instruction without
a bubble. Keep taken-only alignment traps, JALR bit-zero clearing,
link-write suppression on traps, and actual resolved RVFI pc_next.

Preserve the current EX redirect priority over imem backpressure and
the current hold priority for an owner blocked by dmem. A held branch
can keep asserting its repair until advancement; it must retain its
complete instruction and prediction metadata. When it advances, only
the younger combinational fetch slot is annulled. Do not add div_wait
or a generic EX-accept qualifier to the branch recovery cone. Recovery
remains in EX and cannot let a wrong-path instruction reach a memory
owner, retire, or launch DIV/REM. No extra recovery cycle is permitted.

This tests a different recovery boundary from r5s2's control-bank
squashes: the repair-to-ID cone should terminate only at the valid
flop, with no path to decode-control, prediction-metadata, or payload
RESET, CE, or D pins. PC repair remains required. Inspect the mapped
fanout and all three routed seeds to verify this physical claim;
source-level separation alone is insufficient. Also inspect the new
valid-qualified hazard path and the instruction-to-PC target adder.

title: Flatten EX operand selection with direct one-hot forwarding
motivation:
The accepted r5s1 implementation reaches 409.80 fitness at a reported
median 184.06 MHz. Its seed-1 and seed-3 limiting paths run from EX/MEM
destination tags through forwarding selection and JALR resolution to
IF PC bit 1. The current forward_unit encodes a priority decision into
two bits, ex_stage decodes those bits to select each raw operand, and
ALU inputs then pass through separate PC/immediate selection muxes.
This is a small combinational network on several important EX paths.

Prior micro_opt experiments include unsuccessful register-file one-hot
reads (r5s0), JALR alignment precomputation (r6s0), and ALU operation
recoding (r7s0). The structural forwarding-retiming experiment r6s1
retained the encoded 00/01/10 forwarding interface and regressed 8.01%.
None tested direct mutually exclusive forwarding controls combined
with flattened ALU input selection. Their timing regressions also show
that local gate reduction alone cannot establish a fitness benefit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the encoded forwarding-selection network with direct one-hot
source enables and use those enables to flatten EX operand selection.
This is one combinational micro-optimization: no new state, pipeline
boundary, arithmetic operation, predictor, or forwarding source.

For each raw source register, compute the existing live EX/MEM and
MEM/WB matches in parallel:
  E = ex_mem_w_en && ex_mem_rd != 0 && ex_mem_rd == source;
  W = mem_wb_w_en && mem_wb_rd != 0 && mem_wb_rd == source.
Emit a three-bit vector with bit 0 = !(E || W), bit 1 = E, and
bit 2 = !E && W. Thus exactly one of the captured ID operand, EX/MEM
result, and MEM/WB writeback data is selected, preserving youngest
eligible writer priority. Remove the two-bit encode/decode interface
throughout the core; do not generate the new enables by decoding the
old selectors. Keep comparisons combinational at their current stage.

Form each raw forwarded rs value as the OR of its three masked data
candidates. Independently form alu_a from four mutually exclusive
terms: the same three candidates with their enables qualified by
!in.ctrl.is_auipc, plus in.pc qualified by in.ctrl.is_auipc. Form alu_b
analogously using !in.ctrl.alu_src for the three register candidates
and in.imm qualified by in.ctrl.alu_src. Express the four-term merges
as balanced pairwise ORs. In particular, do not implement the ALU
inputs by putting a PC/immediate mux after the raw forwarded bus.
All data and control values remain fully defined, including bubbles;
do not add synthesis don't-cares or technology-specific primitives.

Branch comparison, full-width JALR addition, store data, raw RVFI
operands, and saved divider operands must still use the unmodified
semantic raw rs1/rs2 selections. Keep the ALU operation encoding,
result-selection case, multiplier expressions and sharing, division
arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas, and all result-bank ownership unchanged.
Update div_operands_ready to test the EX/MEM enable bit directly for
either source, retaining its current load-address exclusion only at
divider launch. Do not globally exclude loads from forwarding or
alter the existing load-use interlock and raw-operand RVFI contract.

Preserve the original forwarding producer qualifications. In
particular, use MEM/WB ctrl.reg_write rather than retirement valid or
wb_w_en: an already-retired writer's retained data must still forward
during a dmem hold. Keep trap-suppressed writers ineligible, x0
protected, and all existing reset, flush, redirect, memory-hold, and
divider-wait priorities. The direct normal EX/MEM memory-address bank,
control-zero bubbles, nret=1 ports, and retirement timing are unchanged.

The physical hypothesis is that direct enables remove redundant
priority encoding/decoding on raw forwarding and avoid a serial mux
level on the ALU inputs, shortening tag-to-JALR and tag-to-ALU paths.
Synthesis may already simplify some of the old encoding, and added
enable fanout or different placement may outweigh the reduction.
Inspect the mapped cones and all three routed seeds, including the
competing ALU-result-selection and register-file paths. Preserve one
MULT36X36 and the existing four memory BSRAMs. Missing timing arcs are
unknown delays, not evidence of margin; do not modify timing models.

Predict unchanged CoreMark marker-window cycles and a modest 3% median
Fmax/fitness gain, approximately 422.09 fitness if the supplied winner's
workload and cycle count are reproduced. This is an unmeasured estimate
with low confidence. Require unchanged architectural RVFI streams and
retirement-cycle sequences under identical bus schedules, then use the
existing lint, unit, formal including liveness, ISS cosim, and three-seed
FPGA gates. Keep all CRC, UART, address-bound, and timing-marker checks.
Prior notes distinguish the evaluator's 2 KB workload from supplemental
6 KB runs; disclose the actual measured build and verify the requested
canonical 6 KB workload separately if needed, without changing the
evaluation contract or comparing different binaries across variants.

implementation_notes:
# Flatten EX operand selection with direct one-hot forwarding

Implemented the requested combinational change. Local correctness gates pass,
but the physical hypothesis regresses: median Fmax is 176.40 MHz and fitness
392.74, versus the reproduced baseline's 184.06 MHz and 409.80 (-4.16%).
The predicted 3% improvement was not observed. The implementation is left
for the orchestrator to evaluate; local correctness does not imply acceptance.

## Implementation

- Only `cores/bench/rtl/{forward_unit,core,ex_stage}.sv` changed in RTL.
- `forward_unit` computes live EX/MEM and MEM/WB tag matches independently
  and directly emits `{!E && W, E, !(E || W)}` for each source. The two-bit
  forwarding interface is removed. EX/MEM wins competing matches; x0 is
  excluded through the existing nonzero producer checks.
- `core` connects three-bit `fwd_rs1_en` / `fwd_rs2_en`. Both producer
  qualifications remain `ctrl.reg_write`, including retained, valid-cleared
  MEM/WB writers during dmem holds. No valid, writeback-enable, load, or
  stall qualification was added to the forwarding matches.
- `ex_stage` uses three masked candidates for each semantic raw operand.
  ALU inputs independently merge four masked candidates with balanced
  pairwise ORs, qualifying the register terms with !is_auipc / !alu_src
  and the PC / immediate terms with the corresponding positive controls.
  No RTL mux follows the raw forwarded bus to select the ALU input.
- Divider launch readiness directly tests enable bit 1 on either port.
  The load-address exclusion remains confined to divider launch.
- Branch comparisons, full-width JALR addition, stores, RVFI and saved
  divider operands still consume raw rs1/rs2. Arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas,
  ALU operation/result cases, result-bank ownership, direct memory-address
  register, reset/hold/flush priorities and all top-level nret=1 ports are
  unchanged. No registers, don't-cares or technology primitives were added.

## Tests and equivalence

- Added `test_forward_unit.py`: all 4,194,304 combinations of both source
  tags, both destination tags and both producer enables, plus immediate
  combinational transitions without a clock. Checks exactly-one selection,
  independently different source ports, x0 and youngest-writer priority.
- Adapted `test_ex_result_banks.py` to one-hot controls without removing
  assertions. Added all nine source pairs with independent PC/immediate
  overrides, ADD/MUL in real and ALTOPS modes, every branch comparison,
  full-width JALR carry/alignment cases, raw store/RVFI operands, and all
  four DIV/REM operations with load readiness and saved forwarded operands.
  Existing exact latency, held completion, result ownership, reset and
  inactive-payload checks remain active.
- Extended `test_pipeline.py` with producer distances, competing writers,
  ALU/immediate/AUIPC/branch/JALR/store/DIV/REM consumers, x0, real load-use
  dependencies, trap-suppressed writes, consecutive dependent divisions,
  and 17-cycle dmem holds with overlapping imem stalls and retained WB data.
- All 10 candidate pytest runners passed: 149 cocotb tests across real
  arithmetic, ALTOPS and pipeline configurations. The unchanged baseline
  additionally passed the same 25 pipeline tests.
- Optional `PIPELINE_TRACE_DIR` / `PIPELINE_TRACE_MODE=record` records a
  baseline run; other modes compare. Baseline RTL was copied before edits
  and selected through the existing test helper's RTL/build paths. Exact
  comparison passed for 50 distinct bus schedules, 6,503 retirements,
  1,599 accepted memory effects and 29,990 driven cycles. Every RVFI field,
  retirement cycle, accepted memory cycle/data, final memory and driven
  ready schedule matched. The existing unchanged Python ISS checks also
  passed for these programs.

## Local gates

- Requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings/errors.
- Local formal: **PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed**, including liveness, unique,
  cover and channel-0 checks. Used unchanged `formal/run_all.sh`, automatic
  nret=1 selection, `checks_si.cfg`, `wrapper_si.sv` and bitwuzla, JOBS=4.
  The complete run took about 63 seconds; no RTL fix attempts or formal
  counterexamples. An initial invocation exited before generating checks
  because the default Python lacked PyYAML. Selecting the installed
  Miniconda Python environment resolved this prerequisite issue.
- Existing `tools.eval.cosim.run_cosim`: PASS, selftest and evaluator
  CoreMark ELF. No ISS/harness/evaluation files were edited.
- Unchanged synthesis and FPGA evaluation scripts: all three routed seeds
  completed successfully. Baseline seeds were independently rerun and
  exactly reproduced the supplied winner.
- `formal-deep` was not run: arithmetic is unchanged; real arithmetic was
  exercised by unit tests, directed ISS checks and both CoreMark workloads.

## Routed results and mapped cones

| Variant | Seed 1 MHz | Seed 2 MHz | Seed 3 MHz | Median MHz | Fitness | LUT4 | DFF | MULT36X36 | BSRAM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original snapshot | 184.06 | 191.13 | 179.89 | 184.06 | 409.80 | 5490 | 2112 | 1 | 4 |
| Direct enables | 173.07 | 176.40 | 187.97 | 176.40 | 392.74 | 5531 | 2091 | 1 | 4 |

The synthesized four memory cells remain DPX9B. The 21 fewer mapped DFFs
result from synthesis optimization; RTL state/ownership is unchanged.

Both mapped designs still use 32 final LUT3 cells on each ALU operand,
with mux INIT=0xB8; bit-0 cones retain a MUX2_LUT5 and LUT3 feeding that
final mux. Direct RTL enables did not force a flat physical mux. The
longest structural tag-to-ALU-input path remains five LUT/MUX cells for
both operands. Graph traversal also retains the long ALU arithmetic and
result-selection cone, and the seven-cell RF-to-ID read cone. Structural
counts include primitive dependencies and are not timing measurements.

Baseline seeds 1/3 are limited by EX/MEM rd[0] through forwarding/JALR to
IF PC[1], at 5.43/5.56 ns. Baseline seed 2 is limited by wrapper LFSR[20]
through fetch/register-read selection into ID, at 5.23 ns.

Candidate seed 1 is limited by RF x14[3] to ID at 5.78 ns (2.49 ns logic,
3.29 ns routing). Seeds 2/3 are limited by wrapper LFSR[20] through the
fetch/register-read cone into ID at 5.67/5.32 ns (2.50/2.39 ns logic and
3.17/2.93 ns routing). Thus moving the original limiting cone did not
improve the median timing result.

Additional detailed-report routes reproduced the same three candidate
frequencies. Inspected the normal ALU-result register endpoints as well:
bits 2 and 11 have the largest native detailed-delay entries in seeds
1/2, and bit 5 in seed 3. Reports contain only 11 normal-result bits and
one IF PC bit; unreported paths and missing technology arcs are unknown,
not evidence of timing margin. Native detailed-delay fields are kept
separate from the authoritative final Fmax/critical-path reports. Timing
models and constraints were not modified. A readback-only attempt to
analyze saved PNR JSON crashed in nextpnr's array2d assertion; generating
reports by routing the original synth JSON succeeded reproducibly.

## Workload disclosure

The evaluator actually uses TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=2000, ITERATIONS=10, -O3 and
`--bench --istall --dstall`. That binary reproduced the winner's
**4,491,485 marker-window cycles** (start 15,801; stop 4,507,286). Its UART
passed the existing validator: seedcrc=e9f5, list=e714, matrix=1fd7,
state=8e3a, final=fcaf and `Correct operation validated.` No OOB access.
This 2 KB result alone determines the fitness above.

Separately built the requested TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=6000, ITERATIONS=10, -O3
binary in scratch and ran it on both variants with identical bus seeds.
Both gave **32,836,671 marker-window cycles** (start 56,393; stop
32,893,064), seedcrc=8a02, list=d4b0, matrix=be52, state=5e47,
final=5949, validation literal present, clean EBREAK and no OOB access.
The 6 KB binary is not substituted into the evaluator or compared against
the 2 KB binary. The UART's hardcoded compiler-flags string still says
`-O2 -march=rv32im`; the actual logged build commands use -O3 for both.
CoreMark's printed size is per algorithm: 666 for 2 KB and 2000 for 6 KB.

Complete non-bench RVFI output, including every retirement cycle, was
also streamed and compared by byte count, retirement count and SHA-256
between baseline and candidate for each identical ELF:

| Workload | Retirements | Final retirement cycle | RVFI bytes | Matching trace SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2 KB | 2,937,037 | 4,514,348 | 854,161,634 | d7f581697e844a6001a0b1811d7b3df5e76a0c05a74ab3d5a5dad67b0460be36 |
| 6 KB | 22,093,920 | 32,900,232 | 6,463,986,468 | 34ef03d244b986a66be40660efea1b01b6705ecbf1263bf493d109b7184ac4a0 |

ELF SHA-256: 2 KB `0c13cb0f38ebe9ab87e2f70049e3a0e6dd9ab77b95b612d861951ccc2125361c`;
6 KB `da20d2553fa7fa0237d3ad52dcf40be9444bcaf0e53084e9d302331ada8f30b4`.

## Scope and evidence

No implementation deviations from the hypothesis. Temporary copies,
builds, formal staging, PNR outputs and trace summaries live exclusively
under `$TMPDIR/forwarding-r9s0/`; contract files were read or copied
unchanged. Notes are at the explicitly requested worktree-root path.

Evidence under that scratch directory includes `mapped-cones.json`,
`physical-summary.json`, `routed-endpoint-review.json`,
`coremark-full-trace-equivalence.json`, `pipeline-traces/`,
`validation/{fpga-result,cosim-result,coremark-2k,coremark-6k}.json`,
`validation/formal/last_run-30236.log`, the unit/baseline/candidate test
XMLs, and each variant's `cores/bench/generated/pnr_seed*/` reports.
The full CoreMark streams were hashed while streaming, not retained.

title: Register JALR targets in a two-cycle execute path
motivation:
The accepted r5s1 design reaches 409.80 fitness at 184.06 MHz. Its saved
routed reports identify EX/MEM destination-tag comparison, operand
forwarding, and JALR target generation into the IF PC as the limiting
path in seeds 1 and 3, at 5.43 and 5.56 ns. Seed 2 instead limits on
register-file operand capture. The structural r6s1 forwarding retime,
r7s1 multiply bank, and r8s1 synchronous register file all regressed;
none inserted a register between JALR target arithmetic and PC recovery.
The r6s0 alignment precomputation also regressed, so this experiment
changes execution latency rather than replicating alignment logic.
A dedicated target register could remove the complete live JALR operand
cone from redirect and squash control, at the cost of one extra execute
cycle for each JALR. Whether frequency gain exceeds that cost must be
measured; JALR frequency in the required timed workload is not assumed
to be zero.

r7s1 multiply bank, and r8s1 synchronous register file all regressed;
none inserted a register between JALR target arithmetic and PC recovery.
The r6s0 alignment precomputation also regressed, so this experiment
changes execution latency rather than replicating alignment logic.
A dedicated target register could remove the complete live JALR operand
cone from redirect and squash control, at the cost of one extra execute
cycle for each JALR. Whether frequency gain exceeds that cost must be
measured; JALR frequency in the required timed workload is not assumed

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give legal JALR a blocking, two-cycle EX path. Keep ordinary integer,
multiply, load/store, conditional-branch, and direct-JAL execution at
their existing latency. Use the existing forwarding network and hold
the JALR instruction in ID/EX until completion. This is one structural
experiment in control-transfer execution, with no prediction state.

On the first unstalled EX edge, accept a valid, legal JALR exactly once.
Capture (forwarded_rs1 + immediate) modulo 2^32 with bit 0 cleared into
a dedicated target register, capture the actual forwarded operands for
RVFI, and set a pending bit. Never capture a load address as its rs1
operand; respect the existing load-use interlock and unavailable-load
forwarding qualification. Launch requires the older EX/MEM owner to
be able to advance. It must not depend on target alignment or a live
target-based redirect. Hold fetch and ID/EX on this launch cycle while
allowing older instructions to drain, emitting a control-zero EX/MEM
bubble when that register is available.

During the following cycle, form JALR redirect_target and the alignment
decision exclusively from the registered target. On the next available
EX/MEM edge, consume the pending operation once, emit its instruction
metadata and PC+4 link, and redirect on that same edge if aligned. With
zero bus waits, completion is exactly one clock after launch, adding
one cycle relative to the current JALR. Hold the target, saved operands,
and ID/EX owner if completion is blocked. Reset cancels pending work.
Do not allow live forwarding data or the current JALR adder output to
bypass the target register into PC, squash, trap, or link-write control.

Preserve the current JALR semantics: bit 0 is cleared before alignment
checking, target bit 1 causes the existing misalignment trap, a trapped
JALR suppresses its link and redirect and reports pc_next=PC+4, and an
aligned JALR reports the registered target. A misaligned completion
releases the held sequential fetch normally. Use saved launch operands
for RVFI even after forwarding producers have drained; rd=rs1 and x0
cases must still use the pre-link source value. Illegal JALR encodings
continue through the existing illegal-instruction path without launch.

Add a separate JALR wait input to hazard control. It holds fetch and
ID/EX without retiring or issuing the held instruction twice. Actual
dmem backpressure retains its current priority and preserves the older
request and WB forwarding payload. At aligned completion, clear the
JALR wait condition so redirect can flush the younger instruction and
override an imem stall on the same edge. Restrict the existing live
jump-resolution path to direct JAL; branch behavior is unchanged.
Preserve r5s1's separation between wide payload capture and bubble
control, and retain control-zero invalid EX/MEM entries.

Crucially, advance JALR into EX/MEM only when its registered redirect
is consumed. The r6s2 MEM-stage predictor experiment failed liveness;
do not retire a jump first and redirect one stage later. The proposed
schedule delays JALR retirement together with its redirect, retaining
the existing redirect-to-target-DIV/REM retirement spacing. Verify
that bound with the unchanged formal gate and explicit JALR-to-DIV/REM
streams; do not add divider cycles or relax the liveness window.

Forecast a low-confidence 3% fitness gain. For illustration, a 5% Fmax
gain with 2% more marker-window cycles yields approximately 2.94% more
fitness; these are targets, not measurements. Count timed JALRs and
measure actual extra cycles under identical stall seeds. Register-file,
ALU-control, target-register input, or new hold-enable paths may become
limiting, and added registers may worsen placement. Inspect all three
routed seeds, including target-register input and output paths, without
treating omitted timing arcs as zero delay or adding timing exceptions.

title: Backward prediction with alignment-independent EX recovery control
motivation:
Earlier branch-only prediction reduced the evaluator's marker-window cycles
from 4,491,485 to 4,309,463, but r5s2 and r8s2 lost substantially more Fmax
than they gained in throughput per clock. The r7s2 implementation notes
identify forwarding/JALR alignment followed by repair/hold/squash to ID
control RESET as the worst path in every seed. The r8s2 lesson also shows
that reducing squash fanout to one valid bit did not shorten the upstream
arithmetic cone. Target alignment still participates in the recovery
decision through the shared misalign_fault signal. The full history also
records r6s2's MEM-stage validation failing liveness_ch0, so delaying all
recovery is not an established solution under the unchanged checks.

A misaligned control transfer can request an EX redirect to its existing
architectural continuation, PC+4, while retaining the same trap and link
suppression. This spends a conservative bubble on a trapping transfer
and allows recovery control to depend on decoded instruction class and
branch outcome without waiting for target-alignment qualification.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one static backward-taken conditional-branch predictor with
one-slot EX recovery whose squash strobe is independent of target
alignment. Keep ordinary execution and retirement boundaries unchanged.
The new experiment is the separation of prediction-repair control from
target/trap data selection; the branch policy reuses the measured r5s2
policy. JAL and JALR remain sequentially predicted. Do not add a BTB,
history table, return stack, delayed repair stage, or arithmetic shortcut.

In IF, predecode raw imem_data independently of flush, stall and redirect.
Predict taken only for opcode 0x63, funct3 0/1/4/5/6/7, a negative B
displacement, word-aligned fetch PC, and instruction bit 8 clear. These
conditions guarantee that a predicted branch target is aligned. Compute
its sign-extended B target with full 32-bit modulo arithmetic; compute
PC+4 independently. Select with raw prediction eligibility and apply the
selection only on the existing accepted fetch edge. Reset and EX repair
retain priority. Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC register and
preserve the existing invalid/NOP behavior for discarded fetches.

Carry predicted_taken with the accepted instruction into ID/EX. In ID,
additionally register repair_invert = decoded branch_op[0] XOR
predicted_taken. Keep architectural branch_op unchanged. Treat these
two bits as ordinary payload: synchronous reset, normal capture enable,
and complete retention with a held owner. Their values are inert when
ID/EX valid is zero. Retain the current control-zero invalid entries and
the winner's separate control/payload capture domains; do not introduce
r8s2's raw-invalid-control representation or wide flush-dependent enables.

EX shares equality, signed-less-than and unsigned-less-than predicates
from the existing forwarded operands. Select base_cond by architectural
branch_op[2:1], using equality for BEQ/BNE and the respective less-than
predicate for the signed and unsigned pairs. Architectural branch
direction uses original branch_op[0]. Direction mismatch uses the
registered repair_invert, avoiding a serial extra XOR after direction
selection. Define the recovery request as:

  branch_repair = in.ctrl.is_branch && (base_cond XOR in.repair_invert)
  redirect = in.valid && !reset && !in.ctrl.is_illegal
             && (in.ctrl.is_jump || branch_repair)

Here is_illegal is the registered decoder result, never the dynamically
augmented ctrl_with_trap.is_illegal. Neither misalign_fault, target bits,
target adders, resolved pc_next, nor a full-next-PC equality check may
feed the redirect strobe. No branch_repair_enable alignment qualifier
is needed: taken speculation was already restricted to aligned targets.
Keep recovery level-style through existing holds; do not insert a generic
EX-accept or div_wait qualifier into this strobe.

Preserve existing branch/jump alignment detection, taken-only branch
traps, JALR bit-zero clearing, and suppression of a trapped jump's link
write. These checks still govern architectural ctrl_with_trap and RVFI
pc_next. Separately choose the recovery address. For a decoded jump,
select jump_target when aligned and PC+4 when it traps. For a branch
predicted taken, the only repair is an exit, so select PC+4 directly
from the registered prediction bit. For a branch predicted not taken,
select branch_target when aligned and PC+4 when the taken target traps.
This branch target mux need not wait for the live branch comparison.
All address bits and existing wraparound behavior remain architectural.

In particular, an unpredicted taken misaligned branch and a misaligned
legal JAL/JALR now assert redirect to PC+4 and discard the younger slot.
They retire exactly once with the same trap, suppressed link write and
resolved continuation as today. Never send the misaligned target to IF.
An untaken misaligned branch still does not trap or repair. Reserved
branches, illegal JALR encodings, and invalid entries cannot redirect.
Correctly predicted legal branches have no bubble; an EX repair discards
exactly the one younger combinational fetch/decode slot without stalls.

Preserve PC repair priority over imem unavailability and the existing
dmem/divider hold priority for the resolving owner. A held instruction
keeps its operands and prediction until it advances. A repeated repair
during that hold cannot duplicate retirement or a memory transaction.
Younger stores, loads and DIV/REM must be squashed before they acquire
an EX/MEM or divider owner. Retain existing EX/MEM control-zero bubbles,
held MEM/WB forwarding data, divider completion-bank ownership and the
directly registered memory-address bank. No ALU/divider changes belong
to this predictor hypothesis.

The measurable timing claim is narrower than eliminating all carry
paths: target-alignment and JALR target arithmetic must cease to be
combinational inputs of the squash strobe. Branch comparisons, the
repair-address-to-PC path, ordinary load-use logic and placement remain
potential limits. Inspect mapped dependencies and all three routed
seeds, distinguishing repair control from repair target data; do not
infer success merely from smaller fanout or source-level factoring.

Estimate 3% greater fitness with low confidence. If the earlier 4.0526%
cycle saving survives and median Fmax loses 1%, the product improves
about 3.18%. At 4,309,463 cycles, break-even is approximately 176.60 MHz
against the supplied 184.06 MHz, 409.80 iter/sec winner. These are
conditional forecasts, not measurements; target selection and other
paths may still outweigh the gain. Measure actual marker-window cycles,
median Fmax and resources with the unchanged evaluator. Preserve nret=1
and every hard invariant. Run unchanged lint, unit, formal including
liveness, ISS cosim, CRC/UART, OOB, marker and three-seed FPGA gates.
Explicitly test a misaligned transfer followed by DIV/REM against the
existing progress bound; never change formal depths to accommodate it.
Keep the evaluator fixture authoritative and disclose any 2 KB/6 KB
discrepancy as prior notes do, without modifying the workload or gates.
