title: Factor multiply signedness into one product and one result selection
motivation:
The current winner's r11s0 timing reports put ID/EX alu_op[3] to
EX/MEM normal result bit 23 on the worst path in seeds 1 and 3.
Inspection of the saved mapped netlist shows the path entering a
MUL decode, combining the shared product's low and high halves with
other ALU results, and traversing two MUX2_LUT5 cells before the
normal result register. The RTL describes three signedness variants
of multiplication and four independently selected multiply results.
Yosys already maps them to ONE MULT36X36, so there is no claim that
this proposal removes redundant DSPs. The opportunity is to simplify
multiply control and its contribution to the result-selection cone.

The micro_opt history warns against a broad selector rewrite:
r2s0's registered one-hot ALU tree duplicated the multiplier and lost
5.98% fitness, while r7s0's opcode recoding lost 17.88%. The separate
multiplier register bank in structural attempt r7s1 also regressed.
This experiment instead keeps the existing encoded controls and
register boundaries and changes only the combinational multiply cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three real multiply expressions with one explicitly shared
signed 33-by-33-bit multiplication. Form signed_a only for MULH and
MULHSU, and signed_b only for MULH. Construct signed 33-bit operands
Aext = {signed_a && a[31], a} and
Bext = {signed_b && b[31], b}, then compute one signed 66-bit product
P = Aext * Bext with explicit SystemVerilog widths and signedness.
A zero extension represents every unsigned RV32 operand as a positive
signed 33-bit value; a sign extension preserves its signed value.
Thus P[31:0] supplies MUL and P[63:32] supplies MULH, MULHU and MULHSU.
Bits 65:64 are unused; do not accidentally select P[65:34].

In the real-arithmetic ALU case, group all four multiply opcodes into
one result arm, selecting P[31:0] for MUL and P[63:32] otherwise.
Resolve the high-half signedness entirely at the product inputs:
there should be no post-product selection between three separately
named signedness results. Leave the existing nonmultiply case arms
and default-zero behavior intact. Keep the four exact existing
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS add/subtract-XOR formulas in their guarded branch;
ordinary ALTOPS formal alone cannot establish real-product correctness.

The intended mechanism is fewer distinct multiply terms in the normal
ALU result selection, with sharing explicit before synthesis instead
of dependent on mutually exclusive consumers. No register or pipeline
stage is added. Preserve single-cycle multiply execution, forwarding,
jump-link priority, direct registered memory addressing, all divider
request/response and result-bank behavior, and the nret=1 RVFI contract.
Do not recode ALU operations or add whole-ALU one-hot selection.

Predict unchanged marker-window cycles and a modest Fmax gain. This
is unmeasured and low confidence: synthesis may reconstruct the old
mux topology, input signedness may become critical, or placement may
worsen other paths. Check that the mapped design still has exactly
one MULT36X36 and four memory block RAMs, and inspect connectivity
from both opcode and forwarded operand sources to the product and
EX/MEM result across all three routed seeds. Absence of a modeled DSP
timing arc must not be presented as proof of timing margin.

Validate all four real multiply operations against independent integer
references, then run unchanged lint, unit, formal and ISS cosim gates.
Compare predecessor and candidate with identical binaries and bus
schedules; ordinary instruction and multiply retirement timing should
match. Run the unchanged three-seed FPGA evaluation and separately
verify the requested 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration CoreMark run with its
canonical CRCs, markers and validation literal. Prior logs and the
current benchmark Makefile identify an existing 2 KB evaluator
default; report the two configurations separately and do not alter
benchmark sources or validators to reconcile that discrepancy.

implementation_notes:
# Shared multiply product and result selection

Implemented the requested hypothesis against `hyp-20260906-001-r11s0`, whose RTL commit is `b528e69487651d83e1c0c4b349aac815291d9464`. Local correctness gates pass. The unchanged three-seed FPGA evaluation **regresses median Fmax and fitness by 4.311837265%**, with identical execution cycles. The implementation remains available for the orchestrator's evaluation; the predicted Fmax gain was not observed.

## Implementation

- `cores/bench/rtl/alu.sv`: replaced three real multiplication expressions with signed 33-bit `mul_a_ext`/`mul_b_ext` operands and one signed 66-bit `mul_product`. Operand a is signed only for MULH/MULHSU; operand b only for MULH. The four real multiply case labels share one arm selecting `[31:0]` for MUL and `[63:32]` otherwise. Bits 65:64 are unused under the existing narrowly scoped UNUSEDSIGNAL convention.
- Retained the four exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas, all nonmultiply case arms, default zero, encoded opcodes, interface, and divider connections. No other RTL file changed. No register or pipeline stage was added. Single-cycle multiply, forwarding, jump-link priority, direct registered memory addressing, divider protocol/result banks, and `nret: 1` remain intact.
- `test_alu.py`: retained every existing assertion and added all four multiply operations over a 16-value boundary cross-product and 1,024 deterministic full-width random pairs. Independent Python signed/unsigned integer products check the low/high halves. A second test interleaves multiply variants with every ordinary ALU control and unsupported controls 19 through 31. Both tests also run with the existing exact ALTOPS expectations; all divider latency, arithmetic-state, reset, and held-bank checks remain.
- `test_pipeline.py`: added named high-half instruction encoders, forwarding coverage assertions, and mixed programs for every multiply variant. Coverage includes both EX/MEM and MEM/WB sources on both operands, competing writers, repeated destinations, dependent consumers, x0 writes/reads, load-fed operands, retained WB data, deterministic instruction/data holds, and adjacent DIV/REM operations. Exact ISS, retirement order, PC continuity, accepted memory effects, and existing state-ownership assertions remain mandatory.

No architectural deviation was needed. One new test initially requested a memory/load-use overlap without holding the preceding store. It failed on the unchanged predecessor. Added that store hold to the stimulus and retained the coverage assertion; predecessor and candidate then passed. There were no RTL correctness fixes or formal retries.

## Local validation

- Requested Verilator lint command: pass without warnings/errors, in real and ALTOPS modes.
- Local `bash formal/run_all.sh`: **53 passed, 0 failed on the first proof run**. Used `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=6` and the installed conda Python. The unchanged script auto-selected `wrapper_si.sv` and `checks_si.cfg`. Staged the formal tree under `$TMPDIR` so contract files and the shared upstream checkout were not written.
- All nine candidate pytest runners pass: real ALU 36 cocotb tests, ALTOPS ALU 36, real EX/result-bank 5, ALTOPS EX/result-bank 5, decoder 30, ID 1, immediate generator 8, pipeline 26, register file 5: **152 cocotb tests total**.
- Identical pipeline suites ran on predecessor and candidate using the existing optional trace recorder/comparator. **40 scenarios, 29,936 sampled edges/events, 2,498 launches, and 6,300 retirements match exactly**, including valid RVFI fields, source operands, memory acceptance, bus schedules, resets, dispatches, and cycle numbers. Reset-aborted requests account for launches without dispatch. Both versions independently pass the unchanged Python ISS comparison. Ordinary multiply/integer retirement spacing is one clock; load-use and divide spacing retain their exact previous values.
- The unchanged `tools.eval.cosim.run_cosim` gate passes on both versions for selftest and the evaluator CoreMark binary. Additional selftest runs pass the unchanged ISS at zero waits and with both buses stalled using seeds 1, 2, 3, 19, and 97; all 115 retirements and their cycles match exactly for each schedule.
- The complete real-arithmetic 6 KB CoreMark RVFI streams were compared byte for byte while streaming: **22,093,920 retirements, 6,463,986,468 bytes**, including every emitted operand, result, memory field, and retirement cycle. No difference. Shared SHA256: `34ef03d244b986a66be40660efea1b01b6705ecbf1263bf493d109b7184ac4a0`.

Fast formal uses ALTOPS and does not prove the real product. Real arithmetic is supported here by the independent integer vectors, ISS comparisons, canonical CRCs, and predecessor trace equivalence. `formal-deep` was not run; no claim of a complete real-arithmetic SMT proof is made.

Ran unchanged `make fpga TARGET=bench` on both staged versions with `NRET=1 BENCH=fpga/core_bench_si.sv`. All six routes completed normally. ## Mapped and routed multiply connectivity

Inspected both synthesis netlists and all six routed netlists, stopping combinational traversal at registers and the DSP. Each synthesis contains exactly one MULT36X36 and four DPX9B memories; each route retains one MULT36X36 and four DP memories. All six DSP placements are `X10Y18/MULT36X36`. DSP ASIGN/BSIGN are tied high, clock/enable/reset are tied low, and A/B bits 35:32 repeat the respective bit-32 extension.

- For all 32 bits of both DSP operands, verified connectivity from the corresponding ID/EX source, EX/MEM normal-result bank, EX/MEM divider-result bank, MEM/WB ALU bank, and MEM/WB loaded-data bank. Bit-23 forwarded operand paths have four combinational cells into the DSP in both designs; ID/EX operand paths have three.
- Opcode sources reach both extension bits and normal-result selection. Evaluated the mapped LUT truth tables for all four multiply opcodes and all operand-sign combinations in all eight netlists, with legal multiply `is_jump=0`: 128 cases pass. Yosys/ABC can include jump qualification in optimized multiply-control cones because jump-link data has priority.
- Verified P[i] and P[i+32] each connect to normal EX/MEM result D[i] for every i from 0 through 31, in both synthesis netlists and all routes. DSP outputs 64 through 71 have no combinational path to any normal-result D input. No post-product choice among separately signed products remains in the RTL.
- The routed path from P[23] or P[55] to normal result bit 23 changes from `LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> LUT4` to `LUT4 -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT3` in every seed. Thus one MUX2_LUT5 disappears on that path, but **five combinational cells remain**. Source factoring did not produce a simple reduction in all result-cone depth.

The evidence JSON includes actual cells, ports, placement BELs, and routing-presence information for these paths. These are structural connectivity checks, not sensitized path-delay measurements. They do not establish a timing bound through the multiplier, and absence of a modeled DSP timing arc is not proof of timing margin.

The mapped result cone changes as intended in part, while the measured median regresses. Seed 3 improves, but seeds 1 and 2 regress. Neither a causal timing gain in the multiplier nor multiplier timing margin can be inferred from these reported worst paths. Power and switching were not measured.

## Evidence

All validation scratch files are under `$TMPDIR/multiply-shared-r12s0/`, including `candidate/formal-local.log`, `candidate/units.log`, both `pipeline.log` and `fpga-eval.log` files, lint logs, `protocol-reference/`, `cosim-validation.json`, `selftest-stalled-traces.json`, `sixk-validation.json`, `sixk-full-trace.json`, `fitness-comparison.json`, `mapped-and-routed-multiply-cones.json`, `mapped-sign-truth-tables.json`, six extracted critical-path reports, and `validation-manifest.json`. Staged contract files and tested RTL/tests were checked byte for byte against the worktree. No other core, contract source, benchmark source, or validator was edited.
lesson: - 2026-09-06 hyp-20260906-001-r12s0 (regression, -4.31%): Explicit signed 33x33 multiply sharing in alu.sv kept one MULT36X36 and removed a result-path MUX2_LUT5 but left five combinational cells, while EX/MEM rd-to-JALR/PC forwarding limited all three seeds; reducing multiply mux count did not improve routed timing with unchanged CoreMark cycles.

title: Retime writeback selection into a unified MEM/WB result register
motivation:
The structural history in cores/bench/experiments/log.jsonl shows gains
from changing storage boundaries and ownership: r2s1 separated divider
completion storage, r4s1 moved divider finalization behind registers,
and r5s1 separated pipeline payload capture from squash control. Later
multiplier-bank, register-file, forwarding, JALR, and fetch-queue
experiments regressed routed fitness. In particular, r11s1's frontend
mux and consumption paths erased its modest cycle saving.

The current MEM/WB bundle registers both alu_result and extended
read_data, then wb_stage selects between them with registered
mem_to_reg. That late 32-bit mux feeds the register-file write bus,
same-cycle ID bypass, and MEM/WB-to-EX forwarding. The accepted r11s0
notes report normal EX result selection as critical in two seeds and
MEM/WB tag forwarding through JALR as critical in the other. These
observations do not prove the writeback data mux is the bottleneck,
but motivate reducing downstream data selection and result storage
without adding issue bubbles. No logged structural attempt has moved
this load-versus-execution selection before the MEM/WB boundary.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the two architectural-result fields at MEM/WB with one 32-bit
wb_result register. Perform load-versus-execution result selection on
its D input in mem_stage, using the current EX/MEM owner's mem_to_reg.
wb_stage then exposes wb_result directly as w_data. This is the sole
structural experiment: move one result-selection mux across an
existing register boundary and consolidate its storage, with no new
stage, changed instruction latency, or changed hazard policy.

On each existing !hold_wb capture edge, assign wb_result the value
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result. load_data is the
existing byte/halfword/word extraction and sign-extension result;
in.alu_result already selects the authoritative normal or divider
completion bank. Use the older EX/MEM metadata, never a younger live
opcode or divider response signal. Remove the obsolete registered
alu_result and read_data fields from mem_wb_t rather than retaining
duplicate functional result registers. Keep ctrl_t and its decoding
intact; retaining mem_to_reg in the shared control bundle is harmless
as long as no post-MEM/WB writeback mux still consumes it.

Keep reset synchronous and clear wb_result to zero. A dmem hold must
retain wb_result, destination, and forwarding eligibility along with
the existing MEM/WB payload while clearing retirement valid only.
In particular, never clear or qualify the retained result by valid,
wb_w_en, or a bubble: a stalled EX consumer can still require that
previously retired writer's value. Capture bubbles on the same edges
as before and preserve control-zero invalid EX/MEM entries. Regfile
writes remain gated by valid, reg_write, and the existing x0 rule;
forwarding retains its current producer qualifications and EX/MEM
priority. All consumers, including RVFI rd_wdata, must use the same
unified registered value.

Preserve the exact memory bus transaction and trap behavior. Retain
raw mem_rdata, aligned mem_addr, masks, replicated mem_wdata, and
source operands as independent RVFI metadata; wb_result does not
replace the raw load word. Misaligned loads still suppress writes
and accesses through the existing trap controls. Leave the direct
normal EX/MEM address bank and mem_stage.address connection untouched
so this experiment does not repeat r2s1's RAM-inference failure.
Keep the divider's real and ALTOPS arithmetic, completion bank,
request schedule, top-level nret=1 IO, and retirement order unchanged.

Predict a low-confidence 3% fitness improvement from removing one
downstream mux and up to 32 redundant result-storage bits. With
identical marker-window cycles, any median Fmax gain transfers
directly to fitness. The extra selection before wb_result may instead
make the BRAM-load-to-MEM/WB or execution-bank-to-MEM/WB path critical;
unchanged EX result and JALR paths can also cap or reverse the gain.
These are hypotheses, not measured savings. Inspect mapped result
storage, all three routed critical paths, and RAM inference; disclose
omitted timing arcs instead of treating them as established margin.

Compare against a fresh copy of the accepted core using identical
binaries and bus-stall seeds. Require unchanged lint, existing unit
and ALTOPS checks, formal including liveness and unique retirement,
and stalled ISS cosimulation. Demonstrate cycle-for-cycle equality
of valid RVFI records and accepted memory effects for directed mixed
programs, then compare marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles and median
three-seed Fmax. Require the canonical 6 KB CRCs, validation UART
literal, bounded accesses, and exact markers. The accepted notes
identify 411.53 as the existing evaluator's 2 KB score; keep that
result separate from the required 6 KB comparison, using unchanged

title: Fetch-certified single-entry backedge prediction with registered exit recovery
motivation:
Earlier predictors reduced cycles but lost the frequency needed to improve
fitness. The r7s2 single-entry backedge predictor recorded 192,341 useful
predictions and 12,211 certified exits in its measured marker window, but
its generic stale-hit and immediate recovery logic left forwarding through
JALR alignment and squash critical, reaching only 115.85 MHz. The r11s2
static predictor isolated predicted exits behind a register and recovered
to 169.75 MHz, but suffered 51,941 delayed exits, retained a full-width
instruction-to-fetch target adder, and saved only 2.91% of cycles. These
results suggest testing a selective cached backedge target with a proof
of target identity before speculation and the registered exit mechanism.
This is one predictor experiment on the current 184.84 MHz, 411.53 iter/s
winner; arithmetic, issue width, and the memory architecture stay intact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fully tagged backedge target entry, use it only after the current
raw fetched instruction certifies its target, and repair its not-taken
outcomes through a registered exit event. This specifically replaces the
r7s2 post-speculation certificate and generic stale-hit repair with a
pre-speculation certificate. It also replaces r11s2's stateless fetch
target adder with a registered target and a narrower set of predictions.
It is not a multi-entry BTB, history predictor, return stack, or comparator
redesign. Direct JAL, JALR, and every miss continue predicting PC+4.

The entry holds valid, the complete source PC[31:2], aligned target[31:2],
and all twelve encoded B-immediate bits, including the sign and bit-one
displacement bit. Reset invalidates the entry and cancels pending writes;
its payload need not reset and cannot affect a miss. All address arithmetic
and stored addresses retain the full architectural width. Do not encode
workload PCs, truncate tags to the benchmark memory size, or limit jumps.

In IF, derive eligibility directly from raw imem_data and the PC register,
independent of flush, stall, acceptance, or redirected/NOP-masked payload.
Predict the stored target only when the entry is valid, the entire source
PC matches, the PC is word aligned, and the current instruction is a legal
BRANCH opcode with funct3 in 0,1,4,5,6,7, a negative displacement, and
instruction bit 8 clear. Require exact equality of the current twelve
B-immediate bits with the stored displacement. Otherwise select the
independently computed full-width PC+4. No PC+B-immediate adder is needed
in IF: training stored that exact sum for this exact PC and displacement.
Operands and legal branch predicate may differ from the training branch;
they affect direction, while the certified direct target remains exact.
A changed displacement, illegal encoding, JAL/JALR, DIV/REM, or ordinary
instruction cannot consume a stale prediction. Keep imem_addr connected
directly to the PC register and keep the certificate out of the raw
instruction/regfile-address data path.

Only actual fetch acceptance advances the PC using the selected address.
A prediction never flushes its producing branch. Reset and recovery have
priority, and repair still overrides imem unavailability. Capture the
exact certificate-use bit with the instruction, using pre-edge entry
contents for simultaneous prediction and update, without a write bypass.
ID additionally registers immediate_branch = decoded_is_branch AND NOT
prediction_used. Both bits use ordinary payload capture/hold enables;
invalid metadata is inert. Preserve the winner's independently captured
payload, control-zero bubbles, load-use interlock, dmem/divider holds,
and retained WB forwarding. Never recertify an instruction held in EX
against a newer entry: the certificate refers to its consumed prediction.

Preserve EX's native forwarded comparison and architectural branch_op.
The ordinary immediate redirect substitutes the registered
immediate_branch enable for is_branch in its positive taken-branch term;
retain the existing jump term, validity, and alignment/trap behavior.
Do not add a full next-PC comparison, outcome XOR prediction, generic
stale-hit recovery, or exit-acceptance qualification to that cone. A
correctly taken certified prediction needs neither redirect nor squash.
The pre-speculation certificate guarantees an aligned, exact direct
target, so its only possible error is branch_cond false. RVFI pc_next
always remains the actual resolved next PC, never the predicted target.

Register exit_pending exactly once when a surviving valid, legal certified
branch advances out of EX and resolves not taken. Clear it on every other
clock, including memory holds, reset, and an older registered exit kill.
Use the existing EX/MEM pc_next payload as its recovery address, PC+4 for
this case. Capture that payload with its ordinary enable; the late branch
condition may drive the narrow event flop, not a wide target-bank enable.
On the following cycle the registered event belongs to the older branch
in EX/MEM. Redirect to its registered PC+4, flush the fetched slot and
younger ID/EX owner, and inject a control-zero invalid EX/MEM entry. The
kill wins over younger redirects, load-use holds, and divider holds.
Suppress the killed owner's divider request, response acceptance, effective
div_wait, and training/exit events before the edge. Do not reset the divider
or its completion bank. The recovering owner is a non-memory branch, so
it cannot itself require a dmem hold; an older memory stall had already
deferred that branch's EX advancement and event. Keep dmem hold independent
of recovery to avoid control loops. No younger load/store reaches memory.

Preserve the real delayed-branch retirement schedule demonstrated in
r11s2, rather than repeating r6s2's liveness failure. On the exit recovery
edge, MEM/WB captures the complete real branch record with valid clear and
sets commit_pending. On the next edge it retains that record, presents it
valid exactly once, and clears the pending bit. This consumes the guaranteed
EX/MEM refill bubble without blocking corrected fetch or target execution.
Resume normal WB capture afterward. Reset cancels the pending owner; keep
ordinary memory-hold forwarding behavior. This is a real one-clock delay
of that branch's retirement and all its RVFI fields, not RVFI-only retiming
or a fabricated retirement. No ordinary instruction receives this delay.
A zero-wait corrected DIV/REM immediately after the exit should retire at
most ten clocks after the delayed branch. Check both adjacent retirement
gaps and the unchanged formal liveness check; do not alter divider latency,
ALTOPS, formal bounds, or the retirement contract to make recovery pass.

Train this single entry only from surviving, advancing, legal taken
negative-displacement branches with aligned source and target, including
misses and correctly predicted branches. Register a train_pending pulse
from that EX event and clear it on every non-event clock. On the following
edge, write one coherent tuple from the existing EX/MEM PC, branch_target,
and instruction displacement. Payload write enable uses only registered
train_pending and reset, with no live EX predicate, alignment, or acceptance
fanout and no resident-state read/modify/write. Every replacement writes
all source, target, and displacement bits together. The writing owner is
a non-memory branch and cannot stall in MEM. An older exit suppresses a
younger training event before it is registered. Not-taken branches leave
the entry unchanged. Stale entries are harmless because every use checks
the current raw instruction; retain them until replaced or reset.

Forecast a 3% net fitness improvement with low confidence. As an estimate
only, applying one extra cycle per r7s2 certified exit to its 4,312,067
measured cycles gives about 4.324 million cycles, roughly 3.7% below the
unchanged 4,491,485-cycle predecessor. That saving would require about
178 MHz to break even against today's 184.84 MHz winner. Event counts and
bus-stall alignment will change, so this is not a candidate measurement.
The physical bet is that deleting the IF target adder and generic stale
repair while registering exits leaves enough Fmax for the selective
prediction benefit. Certificate comparison, target mux, registered kill,
deferred-commit fanout, and ordinary pipeline paths remain real risks.

Measure accepted certified hits, correct predictions, delayed exits,
ordinary repairs, and training events on the identical marker-bracketed
workload. Inspect every routed seed for certificate-to-PC timing, event-D
timing, immediate recovery, registered entry-write enables, and commit
fanout. Compute fitness from unrounded iterations/cycle and three-seed
median Fmax. Prior logs identify a 2 KB evaluator versus 6 KB prompt
discrepancy; record the actual workload, preserve all evaluator sources
and checks, and distinguish any supplemental 6 KB result. Preserve nret=1,
external ports, decoder legality, jump links and misalignment traps,
monotonic RVFI order and resolved PC continuity, all M-extension behavior,
result-bank ownership, and the directly registered dmem-address bank.
Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal/liveness, ISS cosim, CRC/UART, OOB,
marker-window, resource, and three-seed FPGA gates during implementation.

implementation_notes:
# Fetch-certified single-entry backedge prediction

Implemented the requested one-entry predictor and registered exit recovery on
`cores/bench` only. The top-level ports and `nret: 1` are unchanged.

## Implementation

- The entry has a complete 30-bit source tag, 30-bit aligned target, all 12
  encoded B-displacement bits, and valid-only reset. One coherent payload
  enable uses only registered `train_pending` and reset. Raw imem data certifies
  legal, aligned negative branches against the complete tuple before use.
  Fetch has an independent 32-bit PC+4 and no PC+B-immediate adder or write bypass.
- ID captures the consumed certificate and decode-folded `immediate_branch`
  with the ordinary payload enable. EX keeps the native forwarded predicate,
  architectural branch controls, jump/misalignment behavior and resolved RVFI PC.
- EX registers advancing, surviving taken-backedge training events and
  certified false-outcome exit events. Registered recovery uses EX/MEM's actual
  PC+4, wins over younger redirects/interlocks/divider holds, and installs an
  invalid, control-zero EX/MEM bubble. It suppresses younger divider launch,
  response acceptance, training and exit events without resetting the divider.
- MEM/WB captures the complete real exit branch with valid clear on recovery,
  retains that record and presents valid exactly once on the next edge, then
  resumes ordinary capture. Ordinary memory-hold forwarding, the independent
  EX payload enable, result-bank ownership and direct dmem address are intact.

## Local correctness

- Requested Verilator lint: PASS, no warnings. `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Unchanged `formal/run_all.sh`, auto-selected single-channel wrapper/config:
  **53 PASS, 0 FAIL**, including liveness, unique, PC continuity and register
  checks. First run passed; zero RTL fix attempts. Final RTL matches the staged
  passing formal sources byte for byte. ALTOPS and all formal depths are intact.
- Full unit suite: **11 pytest runners / 159 cocotb cases PASS**. Both real
  arithmetic and ALTOPS result-bank suites pass. The optional marker observer
  is skipped by the ordinary suite and passed separately when given the ELF.
- New tests exercise every source/certificate bit, full-width wrap/carry,
  legal/reserved predecode, pre-edge collisions, coherent replacements, held
  metadata and pulses, all six predicates, nested conflicting branches,
  changed code, forwarding, memory/imem stalls, killed loads/stores/jumps and
  divider requests, younger training cancellation, and reset of train/exit/
  deferred-commit owners. Complete retirements and accepted memory/divider
  operations are compared against the unchanged ISS.
- Each corrected DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU successor retires exactly **10 clocks** after
  the delayed branch in zero-wait directed tests; the preceding adjacent gap
  is **2 clocks**. Correct hits introduce zero squash slots, ordinary repairs
  one, registered exits two. No original assertion or evaluator check was weakened.
- Unchanged cosim evaluator: **2 ELFs PASS** (selftest full ISS comparison and
  CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB). CoreMark completes with EBREAK, `oob:false`, both
  markers, and the literal `Correct operation validated.`

## Workload and measured events

The actual evaluator builds **TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=2000, ITERATIONS=10, -O3,
RV32IM**, with its unchanged approximately 22% imem/dmem stall generators and
default seed. UART reports a 2K run and per-algorithm CoreMark Size 666. Its
static compiler-flags string still says `-O2`; the actual compile command is
`-O3`. The evaluator and sources were preserved; no supplemental 6 KB run was
performed or substituted for this result.

ELF SHA-256: `14c056a81510bc935a196193d86da02ede3b8f3075acc4d24ee7cd61235f47a6`.
Canonical evaluator CRCs passed: seed `e9f5`, list `e714`, matrix `1fd7`,
state `8e3a`, final `fcaf`.

| Marker-window measurement | Count |
|---|---:|
| Start cycle | 15,675 |
| Stop cycle | 4,339,720 |
| Bracketed cycles | **4,324,045** |
| Accepted certified hits | 204,552 |
| Correct certified predictions | 192,341 |
| Delayed exits / registered recoveries | 12,211 / 12,211 |
| Ordinary advancing immediate repairs | 165,186 |
| Registered training writes | 235,191 |

Events were observed by a test-only C++ subclass around the **included unchanged
`test/cosim/main.cpp`**; no HDL counters or evaluator edits were introduced.
The observer preserves the evaluator's exact cycles, buses, markers and final
retirement and validates its CRC/UART/OOB output again. Training is counted on
the registered write pulse; other EX outcome counts use surviving advancement.

Unrounded iterations/cycle: **10 / 4,324,045 = 0.0000023126493826960636**.
Cycle saving against the supplied 4,491,485-cycle predecessor: **3.7279429854%**.
Break-even frequency against 184.84 MHz: **177.9492701857 MHz**.

## Physical validation

The unchanged three-seed FPGA gate completed successfully, but the hypothesis
**regresses fitness** and does not support the forecast improvement.

| Seed | Routed Fmax (MHz) | Worst path (ns) | Logic / routing (ns) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 86.36 | 11.58 | 5.14 / 6.44 |
| 2 | 91.00 | 10.99 | 4.95 / 6.04 |
| 3 | 91.63 | 10.91 | 5.13 / 5.78 |

Median Fmax: **91.00 MHz**. Resources: **5,684 LUT4-equivalents, 2,231 FFs**;
all three placements/routes succeed within resource capacity. The limiting
paths in every seed begin at EX/MEM forwarding metadata and end at ID/EX
control reset through the ordinary immediate-recovery cone.

Fitness uses the unrounded ratio: `91.00e6 * 10 / 4324045` =
**210.4510938253 iterations/second**, versus the supplied winner's approximately
411.53 iterations/second. Cycle savings cannot compensate for the frequency
loss: **48.86183017% regression**. The unchanged evaluator reports 210.45.
Detailed JSON retains a median of 91.0000915527 MHz; its extra precision does
not change the reported score or conclusion.

Supplemental reroutes with identical device, constraints, seeds and netlist
plus `--report --detailed-timing-report` reproduce all three routed Fmax values.
Every routed seed was inspected. Maximum reported endpoint arrival envelopes
are shown below; these include clock arrival and are **not** the clock-skew/
setup-adjusted critical path delays in the table above.

| Reported endpoint envelope (ns) | Seed 1 | Seed 2 | Seed 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IF PC D, containing target selection/recovery | 12.525 | 11.315 | 11.669 |
| Registered exit event D | 10.984 | 10.298 | 10.153 |
| Immediate-recovery ID control reset | 13.077 | 12.486 | 12.411 |

The report enumerates only two PC D endpoints and does not enumerate isolated
certificate-to-PC, training-event D, payload-CE or commit-CE arrival arcs.
Consequently these numbers do not claim isolated certificate slack or a
complete timing proof for the unreported endpoints. Mapped and routed control
cones were also inspected structurally: all three seeds retain the
same 72-bit registered-only tuple enable, and commit control reaches **321
register CE pins** plus one D and one reset endpoint through combinational
logic. Thus deferred-commit fanout remains substantial even though it is not
the reported global critical path. No routing/check constraints were changed
to compensate for reporting coverage.

Mapped structure inspection confirms 72 unreset predictor payload DFFEs with
one common CE whose only roots are `train_pending.Q` and reset. The predictor
valid bit is separate. No live EX branch predicate reaches the tuple write
enable. Mapped `exit_pending` has 67 direct sinks; `commit_pending` has three
immediate logic sinks before the wide downstream enable fanout above. The
registered-exit cone reaches 216 CE, 188 D and 35 reset endpoints transitively
in each routed seed. The native immediate repair and its squash fanout remain
the dominant measured failure of the physical bet.

## Validation environment and limitations

Validation copies are under `$TMPDIR/hyp-r12s2-validation`. The protected,
shared riscv-formal symlink was copied into this private tree; wrapper/config,
formal runner, benchmark sources, FPGA scripts and ISS/harness were verified
unchanged. The initial scratch `make fpga` resolved Homebrew Yosys 0.64, so
the FPGA gate was repeated with explicit worktree OSS CAD Suite paths
(Yosys 0.64+149, nextpnr 0.10-45-g98c18d7f). The passing formal engine already
used OSS Yosys. No architectural change was made between these runs.

Evidence: `formal-validation.log`, `unit-all-final.log`, `fpga-validation.log`,
`cores/bench/generated/pnr_seed*/nextpnr.log`, `timing-seed*.json` and
`predictor-timing-audit.json` under the validation root. The marker observer's
`metrics.json` and complete `run.log` are in this worktree's
`cores/bench/sim_build/predictor_metrics/`. An attempted routed-JSON reload
hit a nextpnr array-bounds assertion; the successful diagnostic reroutes use
the original synthesis JSON instead. All validation processes have completed.

The original 3% fitness forecast is not a measured improvement: this candidate
passes correctness but is a measured physical regression. Arithmetic, issue
width, memory organization, decoder legality, divider latency and formal
contract were not changed.
lesson: - 2026-09-06 hyp-20260906-003-r12s2 (regression, -48.86%): Certifying cached backedge targets from raw fetch data and registering exits removed the IF target adder and generic stale-hit repair, but EX/MEM forwarding through ordinary immediate recovery to ID/EX control RESET remained critical in every routed seed, limiting median Fmax to 91.00 MHz despite 3.73% fewer 2 KB CoreMark cycles.

title: Remove fetch NOP masking from the instruction data path
motivation:
if_stage currently replaces all 32 instruction bits with ADDI x0,x0,0
whenever fetch is invalid, putting flush/redirect-controlled selection
before register-file addressing, immediate generation, and decoding.
The accepted r5s1 change already made ID/EX payload capture independent
of squashes: id_stage installs zero control and valid=0 for invalid
inputs. The remaining reason for the synthetic NOP is that hazard_unit
compares its source fields without checking fetch validity.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history were checked. r5s1 gained 7.14%
by separating payload from control, whereas r1s0's source-use predecode
required RVFI operand repair. This proposal applies payload/control
separation to the combinational fetch boundary while retaining every
source-field dependency check for valid instructions. Current r11s0
timing reports instead end in ALU result selection in two seeds and
forwarding/JALR in one, so fetch-path simplification is an opportunity
to improve mapping and routing, not an established critical-path fix.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Eliminate only the invalid-fetch NOP data mux. In if_stage, drive
out.instr directly from imem_data on every cycle. Preserve out.pc,
out.valid = !(flush || redirect), and the exact PC update priorities.
Do not replace the removed mux with instruction, source-address, or
immediate masking elsewhere in the decode data path.

In hazard_unit, qualify the existing load_use_hazard expression with
imem_ready && !redirect. These signals are already inputs, and their
conjunction equals current fetch validity because flush_if is
redirect || !imem_ready. Keep both raw source-field comparisons and
the nonzero load-destination guard. No additional opcode predecode,
source-use classification, pipeline register, or core port is needed.
Keep this validity predicate independent of load_use_hazard and stall
outputs so there is no combinational feedback through fetch validity.

The replacement hazard equation is exactly equivalent: when fetch is
valid, old and new logic compare identical fields; when it is invalid,
the old NOP supplies rs1=rs2=0 and therefore cannot match a nonzero
destination, while the new validity guard suppresses the comparison.
All stall/flush/hold decisions should consequently remain identical.
Leave id_stage's existing control-zero bubble handling and synchronous
payload reset intact. Invalid payload may contain arbitrary instruction
bits, but it must never own execution, forwarding controls, a redirect,
a divide request, a memory transaction, or a retirement. Holds must
still retain the complete active instruction and retained WB data.

Expect unchanged instruction timing and marker-bracketed CoreMark
cycles, with a low-confidence 3% fitness gain from Fmax. Removing wide
instruction masking may reduce decode-path logic and redirect fanout;
the added hazard qualification or changed placement may instead erase
the gain. Inspect mapped instruction/address cones and all three routed
seeds to test that mechanism. Preserve nret=1, decoder legality, all
RVFI fields on valid retirements, arithmetic and ALTOPS behavior, the
eight-clock divider, and the directly registered memory-address bank.

Require unchanged lint, unit, formal, and stalled ISS cosimulation
gates. Compare accepted-core and candidate valid RVFI records, their
cycles, fetch addresses, and accepted memory effects with identical
binaries and bus-stall schedules. Validate the canonical 6 KB CRCs,
UART validation literal, bounded accesses, and exact timing markers.
Use the unchanged median-of-three FPGA evaluator. Existing r11s0 notes
distinguish its 2 KB evaluator score of 411.53 from the canonical 6 KB
run; report matching workloads separately if that discrepancy persists,
without changing any benchmark, wrapper, validator, or contract file.

title: Move high-half multiplication behind the blocking M-extension boundary
motivation:
The current winner's saved r11s0 timing reports identify ID/EX alu_op
through normal ALU result selection as the worst path in two seeds;
forwarding through JALR limits the third. The structural history shows
that moving division out of single-cycle execution succeeded, whereas
r7s1's same-cycle multiply bank regressed 6.73% and r12s1's unified
writeback register regressed 14.04%. Merely moving result muxes has not
reliably improved routed timing.

Static disassembly of the winner's saved 6 KB CoreMark ELF finds twelve
MULHU instructions, all in core_list_init or ee_printf, and no MULH or
MULHSU. Matrix functions use ordinary low-half MUL. This suggests that
high-half multiplication can tolerate extra latency without slowing
the timed computation; it is not a measured dynamic instruction count.
The opportunity is to remove the three high-product choices and their
signedness handling from the common execution path while retaining
single-cycle MUL. Existing results already show one shared MULT36X36,
so this proposal does not claim redundant multipliers currently exist.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Execute MULH, MULHU and MULHSU through the existing blocking M-extension
request/completion path, with registered operands and two post-request
compute clocks. Keep all RV32I operations and low-half MUL on their
current single-cycle path. This selective execution-latency split is
the sole architectural change; it applies to every instruction stream
solely by decoded opcode, without recognizing benchmark PCs or data.

In alu.sv, retain a combinational unsigned low-32-bit product for MUL
and remove the combinational high-half and signed-product result arms
from the normal ALU output. High-half opcodes return zero on that
inactive normal output and obtain their architectural results only
through the blocking path. Preserve all nonmultiply arithmetic and
the current DIV/REM interface and real arithmetic.

Extend div_unit's existing ownership protocol with a registered
high-multiply mode. On an accepted high-multiply request, retain raw
A and B plus signedness: A is signed for MULH/MULHSU, B only for MULH.
Reuse the idle-captured dividend/divisor storage where possible;
divisor magnitude already equals raw B for these nondivision opcodes.
Existing DIV/REM normalization and saved operands must remain exact.
Form signed 33-bit operands by sign or zero extension as selected by
the saved mode, and compute their signed 66-bit product using only
registered operands. The required high word is product[63:32].

If the request is accepted at edge R, capture that high word in a
private product register at R+1. At R+2, copy this already registered
word into the existing result_q completion bank and, if unblocked,
accept the matching EX/MEM metadata on the same edge. Set the terminal
interval for high multiply to count==1; retain count==7 and the exact
eight-clock schedule for DIV/REM. Product payload may capture freely
outside ownership; avoid adding request/legality qualification to its
wide data enable. All completion selection uses registered mode and
data, never live forwarded operands or the live opcode.

Preserve the held-response protocol. result_q changes only on a
completion or reset, remains stable after consumption, and survives
subsequent idle operand captures and request acceptance. A blocked
response retains its result until accepted. Reuse the current single
EX/MEM slow-result selector for both instruction families, rather than
introducing a third result bank into the forwarding mux. Keep the
normal registered memory-address connection independent of this mux
so block-RAM address-register absorption remains possible.

In EX, classify high multiplies alongside divisions for launch,
active ownership, source snapshots, waiting and acceptance. Launch
once with usable forwarded operands and no older memory hold. Hold
ID/EX and fetch while allowing older stages to drain once; preserve
an actually stalled EX/MEM owner. The existing div_wait interface can
carry this generalized wait without changing hazard priorities.
Capture the original PC, rd and exact operand values for retirement.
Normal forwarding must consume the common registered completion bank
on the following cycle, including consecutive mixed slow operations.

Keep ALU_MUL's existing ALTOPS formula on the combinational path.
Move the exact MULH/MULHU add-XOR and MULHSU subtract-XOR formulas to
the high-multiply protocol, using the same two-clock schedule as real
hardware. Preserve every DIV/REM formula and its original schedule.
Decoder legality defaults, traps, memory handshakes, nret=1 ports,
in-order retirement and the formal liveness bound remain unchanged.

Predict a low-confidence 4% fitness gain from simplifying the common
ALU selection and separating high-product computation from forwarded
operands. Expect no added timed high-multiply bubbles only if dynamic
profiling confirms the static workload observation. An additional
multiplier, product register and completion mux can instead worsen
placement or create a new limiting path; ordinary JALR can still cap
Fmax. Report actual DSP use, potentially two MULT36X36 equivalents
instead of one, and require successful placement on the same device.

During implementation, run unchanged lint, unit, formal/liveness,
real-arithmetic ISS cosim and three-seed FPGA gates. Inspect both
common-ALU and new registered-product paths across all routed seeds;
missing timing arcs are not timing margin. Profile retired multiply
classes strictly between markers and compare the same binaries and
bus-stall configurations. Preserve the canonical 6 KB CRCs, validation
literal and OOB checks. Prior logs identify a pre-existing 2 KB
evaluator default: report its result separately from the requested
6 KB run without changing benchmark sources, validators or constraints.

title: Bimodal direct-branch prediction with fully registered recovery
motivation:
The predictor experiments repeatedly saved instructions' recovery slots but
lost more fitness through routed timing. The r11s2 asymmetric predictor
registered exits and passed liveness, yet retained immediate EX recovery;
r12s2's surviving immediate-recovery path limited all three routed seeds to
roughly 91 MHz. The r6s2 all-MEM-recovery BTB failed the unchanged liveness
check before obtaining physical results. This proposal combines a small
direction-only predictor with a complete register boundary on recovery and
an explicit architectural commit schedule for recovering control transfers.
It tests whether eliminating the remaining live EX-to-squash path can make
useful prediction survive the frequency-times-throughput fitness metric.

The predictor experiments repeatedly saved instructions' recovery slots but
lost more fitness through routed timing. The r11s2 asymmetric predictor
registered exits and passed liveness, yet retained immediate EX recovery;
r12s2's surviving immediate-recovery path limited all three routed seeds to
roughly 91 MHz. The r6s2 all-MEM-recovery BTB failed the unchanged liveness
check before obtaining physical results. This proposal combines a small

It tests whether eliminating the remaining live EX-to-squash path can make

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one 64-entry bimodal conditional-direction predictor with fully
registered control-transfer recovery. Compute direct targets from the
current fetched instruction. Early direct-JAL steering belongs to this
same front end; JALR uses sequential prediction and registered recovery.
Keep ordinary pipeline depth and the existing arithmetic resources.

Index 64 two-bit saturating counters with the full fetch PC's bits [7:2].
Reset counters to weakly not taken (01); their MSB predicts direction.
The table is deliberately untagged: aliasing changes prediction accuracy,
never architectural targets or legality. A raw fetch predecoder admits
only BRANCH opcode 0x63 with funct3 0/1/4/5/6/7, or JAL opcode 0x6f.
Require a word-aligned source and target for taken prediction. For these
aligned source PCs, B-immediate alignment is instruction bit 8 clear and
J-immediate alignment is instruction bit 21 clear. Predict an eligible
conditional branch taken when its counter MSB is set, and an eligible JAL
taken unconditionally. Compute the exact B/J sign extension and full
32-bit PC-relative target modulo 2^32. Compute PC+4 independently.

Select the target using raw predecode/table outputs independently of
stall, flush, redirect, and acceptance. These controls govern PC capture,
not the prediction data select. Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC
register. Only actual fetch acceptance may apply a prediction. Carry its
consumed predicted_taken bit and two-bit counter snapshot with that same
instruction into ID/EX; holds retain the complete metadata. A prediction
must not squash its own instruction. Raw predecode uses the current
imem_data, so stale direction state cannot steer ordinary, illegal, or
misaligned instructions to a cached address. There is no stored target,
target tag comparison, return stack, or speculative history rollback.

EX preserves the existing forwarded predicates, exact branch/jump targets,
JAL/JALR link results, taken-only alignment faults, and actual pc_next.
For a direct branch or JAL, its consumed prediction is wrong when the
predicted_taken bit differs from the actual legal, aligned transfer
decision. A direction difference may conservatively repair even if the
direct displacement happens to equal +4. Every legal aligned JALR requests
recovery to its existing resolved target. Illegal encodings and invalid
entries cannot recover; a misaligned transfer keeps the existing trap,
suppressed jump link, and sequential continuation. A predicted direct
target is exact by construction, so no generic full-next-PC comparison
is needed and a load, store, or DIV/REM can never own prediction recovery.

Register recovery_pending only when the resolving control instruction
actually advances from EX, with reset, memory hold, and older recovery
cancellation handled explicitly. Clear the event on every non-event
clock. Reuse EX/MEM's architectural pc_next as the recovery address,
captured with the ordinary payload enable independently of the event.
Remove ALL immediate EX redirects, including unpredicted conditional
branches, JAL, and JALR. The live branch comparison, forwarded JALR target,
legality, alignment, and direction-mismatch cones must terminate in
registers before affecting PC recovery, fetch masking, ID squash, or
younger-EX cancellation. This complete cut is the distinguishing timing
experiment; retaining an ordinary immediate-repair fallback defeats it.

In the next cycle recovery_pending belongs to the older EX/MEM control
instruction. Its registered target overrides younger predictions and
redirects fetch even when imem is unavailable. Kill the younger ID/EX
owner before EX/MEM capture, clear its complete controls and validity,
and flush the younger combinational fetch slot. Suppress its divider
request, response acceptance, effective div_wait, training, and recovery
event. A killed younger divide cannot already have launched: it entered
EX on the edge that registered this older recovery event. Do not reset
the divider or disturb its registered completion bank. The recovering
control instruction has no memory request, so dmem readiness cannot hold
it. Keep dmem-stall generation independent, and give registered recovery
priority over younger load-use/divider holds. Correct predictions incur
no squash; a recovery discards two younger slots under zero wait.

Make a real one-clock postponement of the recovering instruction's
writeback/retirement part of this recovery protocol. On the recovery
edge, MEM/WB captures its complete architectural record with valid clear
and sets commit_pending. On the next edge retain that record, assert
valid once, and clear commit_pending; normal capture resumes afterward.
The overwritten incoming MEM record is necessarily the invalid EX/MEM
bubble injected by recovery. Corrected fetch and execution continue
during this commit delay. For a JAL/JALR owner, its link write occurs
on this same actual WB-valid schedule, with the ordinary forwarding
paths exposing the correct link to its target. All RVFI fields and
regfile write enable must identify this real owner and its valid cycle.

Apply deferred commit only to the recovering branch/jump, never an
arithmetic or memory owner or a correctly predicted transfer. With the
event captured at edge E0, recovery occurs at E1 and the real owner is
valid in MEM/WB at E2. A corrected DIV/REM successor launches at E3,
accepts at E11, and becomes valid in MEM/WB at E12: a ten-clock adjacent
retirement gap. Check both neighboring gaps, including a predecessor
DIV/REM and a recovering JALR with forwarding. Preserve the existing
formal liveness bound, ALTOPS timing, and eight-compute-clock divider;
fabricated retirements or RVFI-only delay are forbidden. Reset cancels
pending recovery and commit ownership. Existing memory-hold WB operand
retention remains intact.

Train each surviving, legal conditional branch once on EX advancement,
using the actual outcome to saturate its saved counter snapshot. Capture
train_pending and the resulting two-bit value into registers, reusing
EX/MEM source PC for the index. The next clock writes the table using
only this registered event, index, and value. A recovering branch may
train; its killed successor may not. Do not train repeatedly during
holds or add a combinational update-to-lookup bypass. Lookup observes
pre-edge state. An aliased or old counter snapshot is an accuracy loss,
not a correctness hazard. Table payload/reset cost must be measured.

Forecast a 4 percent net fitness gain with low confidence. For example,
five percent fewer cycles with one percent lower Fmax yields about
4.21 percent improvement; at that cycle saving the 184.84 MHz winner's
break-even frequency is about 175.60 MHz. These are conditional targets,
not measurements. Two-slot misses, small-table aliasing, the IF target
adder, and deferred-commit fanout can erase the gain. Historical cycle
counts include a documented 2 KB evaluator fixture and must not be
represented as measured 6 KB results. Record the actual evaluated ELF,
working set, marker-window cycles, accepted predictions, both direction
errors, JALR recoveries, and table writes. Preserve the required 6 KB
CRC/UART/OOB/marker checks and report any existing fixture discrepancy
explicitly without changing benchmark sources or evaluator contracts.

Inspect mapped dependencies and every routed seed: no live EX predicate
or target-alignment cone may reach fetch/ID squash without crossing
recovery_pending. Also inspect recovery-event D, table lookup-to-PC,
counter-write controls, recovery fanout, and commit enables; moving the

implementation_notes:
Implemented the 64-entry bimodal direct-branch predictor and fully registered recovery. Correctness gates pass. The forecast fitness gain was not achieved: the measured three-seed median is 140.61 MHz, and the 2 KB evaluator fitness is 329.6216418960102 iterations/s. The separately measured required 6 KB workload yields 45.03360898496885 iterations/s. Neither number uses the evaluator's rounded `ipc_coremark` field.

Changes:

- Added 64 untagged two-bit counters, indexed by fetch PC[7:2], reset to 01. The table has no target storage, tags, bypass, or speculative history.
- IF validates current raw BRANCH funct3/JAL encodings and source/displacement alignment. A shared full-width B/J target adder uses the raw opcode-selected signed immediate; PC+4 has an independent adder. Prediction data selection is independent of stalls, acceptance, flush, and recovery. Only fetch acceptance advances by prediction, and imem_addr remains the PC register itself.
- IF/ID and ID/EX carry consumed predicted_taken and the two-bit snapshot. ID payload capture remains independent of validity/control flush; holds preserve every payload field and all prediction metadata.
- EX computes actual predicates, targets, traps, links, and architectural pc_next as before. Direct direction mismatch and every legal aligned JALR generate recovery only when the control owner advances. All immediate EX redirects were removed. recovery_pending clears on every non-event edge, including holds and older cancellation.
- The registered event kills the younger EX owner, suppresses divider launch/accept/wait and predictor events, clears EX/MEM controls/validity, flushes ID and the combinational fetch slot, and redirects using EX/MEM.pc_next even when imem is unavailable. Memory backpressure remains independently computed. The divider resource, completion bank, eight-compute-clock protocol, arithmetic, and direct normal memory-address bank are unchanged.
- On recovery E1, MEM/WB captures the entire recovering record invalid and sets commit_pending. At E2 that same record is retained and becomes valid once. Regfile write enable and RVFI use that real MEM/WB-valid schedule; existing forwarding exposes jump links to corrected successors. The overwritten E2 incoming record is the invalid recovery bubble. Correct fetch proceeds during the delay. Reset cancels both event and commit ownership.
- Conditional training is registered once per advancing surviving nontrapping branch, using its saved snapshot and actual outcome. The next edge writes using registered train_pending/train_value and EX/MEM source PC. Killed successors and held owners cannot train. Untaken branches with unaligned displacements remain legal and can train not taken.
- Hazard outputs use independent continuous assignments. The load-use inputs use exactly the same masked raw instruction bits as IF, avoiding a packed-metadata dependency cycle in Verilator's public-signal simulation mode without changing architectural behavior.

Tests and local gates:

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings. Public-flat-rw lint also passes without warnings. git diff --check and the unchanged channel-0 contract scanner pass.
- Final unchanged pytest entry point over cores/bench/test: 11 runners passed, 156 cocotb cases passed, including both real and ALTOPS arithmetic/result-bank suites. Pipeline cases include many directed subcases, including all 96 combinations of six taken predicates and four DIV/REM predecessor/successor operations, plus 16 JALR and 16 direct-JAL combinations.
- New table/fetch tests cover all entries/states, reset/write precedence, no pre-edge bypass, aliasing, all branch funct3 values, changed instructions, JAL/JALR distinctions, source/target alignment, signed full-PC carries/wrap, and prediction selection while acceptance is blocked.

They cover both direction errors, zero-slot hits, two-slot repairs, killed stores/loads/divides, forwarded links and changing JALR targets, long imem/dmem holds, consecutive repairs, and reset in both recovery and commit phases.
- Recovering branch/JALR following DIV/REM: adjacent retirement gap 2. Corrected DIV/REM after recovery: gap exactly 10. With E0 event registration, recovery E1, owner valid E2, corrected divide launches E3, accepts E11 and is valid E12. Existing maximum-ten-clock and eight-compute-clock assertions remain enforced. Correctly predicted JAL has predecessor gap 1 and divide-successor gap 9.

Its defensive unpredicted-recovery case is exercised directly at EX, including displacement +4; full-pipeline JAL tests check the naturally reachable correct-prediction case. No fabricated retirement or prediction fault injection was used.

title: Share logical and arithmetic right shifts through sign injection
motivation:
The accepted core expresses SRL and SRA as separate variable shifts and
separate ALU result arms. Their only semantic difference is the bit
shifted into the vacated positions. Explicitly sharing this operation
can reduce shift logic and result-selection fan-in without changing
any instruction latency or adding a pipeline control dependency.

The saved r11s0 implementation notes and accepted routed reports show
alu_op[3] through normal ALU result selection limiting seeds 1 and 3;
the mapped path also crosses shift-amount-controlled selection before
normal EX/MEM result bit 23. Seed 2 is limited by forwarding to JALR.
This supports examining the common result cone, but does not establish
that a barrel-shifter data path itself is currently critical.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history record regressions from broad
one-hot ALU selection in r2s0, operation recoding in r7s0, and explicit
multiply sharing in r12s0. No prior hypothesis specifically merges
SRL and SRA. The proposed sharing is local to these two operations;
its benefit depends on what the existing synthesis already shares.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement SRL and SRA with one combinational arithmetic right shifter
in alu.sv. Form a signed 33-bit input consisting of one fill bit
concatenated with the unchanged 32-bit operand a. Set the fill bit
to a[31] only when op equals ALU_SRA, and otherwise to zero. Apply a
single signed arithmetic right shift by b[4:0], then use its low
32 bits as the shared result. For SRL the added zero bit makes the
widened value nonnegative; for SRA the added sign bit preserves its
signed value. Shift amount zero must return a for both operations,
and all upper bits of b remain irrelevant.

Group ALU_SRL and ALU_SRA into one output-case arm selecting this
shared result. Keep the 33-bit intermediate explicitly signed across
concatenation and shifting, with explicit final slicing to avoid
accidental logical shifting, implicit truncation, or width warnings.
Remove the two old right-shift expressions so they cannot survive as
parallel functional datapaths. Keep SLL and every other operation's
expression and result arm unchanged. In particular, preserve the
existing multiply expressions, their case structure and ALTOPS
formulas, the encoded ALU operation values, and the complete divider
interface and eight-clock ownership protocol.

This is a single local datapath-factoring experiment. It introduces
no registers, operand forwarding, control sidebands, clock enables,
or instruction-dependent stalls. All pipeline capture and hold
behavior, normal registered memory addresses, instruction legality,
trap handling, bus handshakes, nret=1 ports and RVFI values remain
equivalent. Changes are confined to cores/bench RTL and unit tests.

Predict an unmeasured 3% fitness improvement, with low confidence,
from reduced mapped right-shift/result-selection logic and routing.
Marker-bracketed cycles should be identical for identical binaries
and stall schedules, so a frequency improvement transfers directly
to fitness. Sign injection can instead add a limiting control path,
synthesis may already share most of the original shifts, or the
unchanged forwarding/JALR cone may cap Fmax. Inspect the mapped cone
and all three routed seeds; do not infer timing margin from missing
arcs or assume that fewer source expressions guarantee fewer LUTs.
Check that the existing single MULT36X36 mapping and memory inference
survive this local change.

During implementation, require unchanged lint, unit tests, formal
including liveness and unique retirement, and real-arithmetic ISS
cosimulation. Compare complete valid RVFI records and their cycles
against the accepted core with identical bus-stall schedules. Run
the unchanged three-seed FPGA evaluation and the canonical 6 KB
CoreMark comparison with exact timing markers, CRCs, UART validation
literal and bounded memory accesses. The saved accepted notes report
a pre-existing 2 KB evaluator default; report that score separately
from the requested 6 KB run if it persists, without modifying any
benchmark, evaluator, wrapper, constraint, or other contract file.

# Shared logical/arithmetic right shift

Implemented against accepted RTL at HEAD `36a86f9fea970a0f0ee46fab70ab5345cd6488aa` (current source ID `hyp-20260906-001-r11s0`). Correctness and cycle-equivalence checks pass. The measured three-seed median Fmax falls from **184.84 to 176.80 MHz**, reducing fitness **4.349707855%**. The proposed low-confidence 3% improvement was not observed; this implementation remains the requested local factoring experiment.

## Changes and scope

- `cores/bench/rtl/alu.sv`: added explicitly signed 33-bit input/result signals. The input is `$signed({(op == ALU_SRA) && a[31], a})`; a single `>>> shamt` supplies the low 32 bits to a grouped `ALU_SRL, ALU_SRA` case arm. Both old right-shift expressions are removed. Comments explain the signed width and exact shift-zero behavior. The unused result bit 32 uses the existing local `UNUSEDSIGNAL` convention.
- SLL, every other expression/result arm, all multiply expressions and ALTOPS formulas, operation encodings, divider wiring and eight-clock protocol are unchanged. No sequential RTL, pipeline capture/hold behavior, memory-address register, forwarding, decode, trap, handshake or RVFI logic was edited. `nret` stays 1.
- `cores/bench/test/test_alu.py`: retained every existing assertion and added 138 operands crossed with all 32 shift amounts and five independently varied upper-b patterns. Operands include zero, all ones, signed extrema, walking ones/zeros, mixed patterns and 64 deterministic random values. Independent Python unsigned/signed references check SRL/SRA while repeatedly alternating SRL, SRA, SLL, ADD, XOR and LUI without clock edges. Each real/ALTOPS build executes 176,640 additional combinational checks, including 88,320 right-shift checks, and verifies unchanged divider state.
- `cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py`: added register/immediate right-shift encoders and two directed tests. Coverage includes EX/MEM and MEM/WB sources for both register operands, competing operand/destination writers, retained WB load forwarding, load-use interlocks, overlapping instruction/data waits, negative operands, amounts 0/31, ignored upper register-shift bits, x0 destinations, dependent stores, taken/untaken branches and killed stores. A second program sweeps every amount and checks register versus immediate results and stored values. Existing protocol/ISS/trace support and all prior assertions remain.

No architectural deviation was needed. Validation used isolated copies under the existing `$TMPDIR` so generated formal, benchmark and simulation artifacts did not modify contract files or another core. The installed conda Python provided the existing validation dependencies. No benchmark/evaluator/wrapper/constraint/helper source was edited.

## Local correctness status

- Requested `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP -sv +incdir+cores/bench/rtl cores/bench/rtl/*.sv`: **pass, no warnings/errors**. The same lint command with `-DRISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` also passes.
- Local `bash formal/run_all.sh`: **53 passed, 0 failed**, including `liveness_ch0`, `unique_ch0`, instruction, register, PC, illegal and cover checks. Environment: `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=4`, conda Python on PATH; unchanged script auto-detected `nret=1` and selected the unchanged single-retirement wrapper/config. **First proof attempt passed; zero RTL fixes/retries.** No counterexample occurred.
- All **nine pytest runners / 150 cocotb tests pass**: real ALU 35, ALTOPS ALU 35, decoder 30, real EX 5, ALTOPS EX 5, ID 1, immediate generator 8, pipeline 26, register file 5. The new pipeline tests passed on the accepted RTL before the shifter edit.
- The accepted pipeline suite recorded `PIPELINE_TRACE_MODE=record`; the candidate used `compare` with the same trace directory. **41 scenarios, 31,408 sampled edges/events, 7,632 valid retirements, 2,450 divide launches and 2,051 accepted memory effects match exactly.** The comparison includes complete valid RVFI records, cycles, ready schedules, requests/accepted effects, divider operands/results and resets. Every protocol scenario independently passes the unchanged Python ISS comparison and existing ownership/latency assertions.

## Mapped cones and all routed critical paths

Pre-mapping Yosys inspection confirms that the accepted ALU has a 32-bit `$shr` and a signed 32-bit `$sshr`, whereas the candidate has exactly one signed 33-bit `$sshr` (`A_SIGNED=1`, `A_WIDTH=Y_WIDTH=33`, `B_WIDTH=5`). The unsigned 32-bit SLL remains unchanged.

Structural traversal of actual normal-result register D cones, stopping at registered/macro boundaries, finds an `alu_op[3]` to normal result bit 23 path of seven combinational cells in the accepted netlist and nine in the candidate. title: Isolate all multiplication behind a registered operand boundary
motivation:
The accepted core still routes all four combinational multiply results
through its normal ALU selection after operand forwarding. Prior structural
attempts identify two incomplete separations: r7s1 added an output bank
without registering multiplier inputs and lost 6.73% fitness; r13s1 moved
only high-half operations to the blocking resource, doubled MULT36X36 use,
and lost 4.38%, with normal ALU selection still critical in two seeds.
Moving the entire multiply family across an operand register boundary can
remove both the DSP and multiply selection from the common execution path
while retaining one physical multiplier. Low-half MUL occurs in CoreMark,
so its added execution cycle must be charged to measured fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Execute MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU through the existing blocking resource
and registered completion bank, using one post-request compute clock for
multiplication. This is the sole structural change. Preserve single-cycle
RV32I execution, the current eight-compute-clock DIV/REM implementation,
pipeline retirement boundaries, instruction legality, and nret=1 ports.

Remove every real multiply expression and every multiply result arm from
alu.sv's normal combinational output. Those opcodes must obtain results
exclusively through the blocking protocol; their inactive normal output
is zero. Keep the ordinary ALU encoding and compact case selection intact.
Inside div_unit.sv, implement one explicitly shared signed 33-by-33 product
of registered operands. Extend A with its sign bit for MULH/MULHSU and
with zero for MUL/MULHU; extend B with its sign bit only for MULH. Register
those extension bits with the exact raw 32-bit operands on the request
edge. Select product[31:0] for MUL and product[63:32] for the other three
operations using a saved high-half flag. A signed 66-bit product preserves
all four RV32M results. Do not instantiate separate products per opcode.
Reuse existing idle-captured raw dividend/divisor storage where ownership
permits, but preserve DIV/REM magnitude normalization and saved signs.

If a multiply request is accepted at edge R, only registered operands and
registered operation metadata feed the multiplier during R to R+1. Assert
its terminal response during that interval and capture the product slice
in the existing result_q at R+1. On the same edge, EX/MEM can accept the
matching instruction metadata and select that newly written result bank.
There is no intermediate product register or additional finish edge:
successive unstalled multiplies accept EX/MEM two clocks apart, adding
one EX occupancy clock per MUL-family instruction relative to the parent.
DIV/REM still complete on the eighth post-request edge and successive
divides remain nine clocks apart. Use a saved operation-class bit and
class-specific terminal count; never let the live opcode choose an active
operation's completion time or result. Normal result forwarding remains
available immediately after EX/MEM acceptance.

Generalize EX's existing divide ownership, request, operand snapshots,
wait and acceptance to all eight M-extension operations. Launch exactly
once from a valid legal owner with usable forwarded operands and no older
memory hold. Hold ID/EX and fetch until acceptance while draining older
stages once. Retain a genuinely stalled memory request and the existing
valid-cleared MEM/WB forwarding payload. Both actual source values and
instruction metadata must survive changing live inputs during execution.
Reset cancels pending work and unconsumed responses; killed instructions
and bubbles never launch. Preserve the current held-response behavior and
safe simultaneous held-response consumption/request refill at the unit
interface. result_q changes only on completion or reset and survives
consumption, idle captures and subsequent launches. Reuse the existing
EX/MEM slow-result selector for both multiplication and division, keeping
a single selected registered value for forwarding and MEM/WB. Leave the
independent normal memory-address bank directly connected to MEM so BRAM
address-register absorption is preserved.

Move the exact four multiply RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas into the same
registered-operand protocol, with the same one-compute-clock schedule as
real multiplication. Preserve every existing DIV/REM formula, arithmetic
vector and eight-clock assertion. Retain trap, alignment, x0, RVFI operand,
consecutive retirement-order, and bus-handshake behavior. Passing ALTOPS
proves neither the product signedness nor real arithmetic; require exact
real-result tests and unchanged ISS cosimulation as well.

Forecast a low-confidence 4% fitness gain. The intended source is a shorter
common ALU cone and isolated DSP inputs, not free multiply throughput.
Measure the retired multiply count M strictly between timing markers and
the parent's bracket length C. M/C is a first-order added-cycle estimate
before imem/dmem stall overlap; use actual candidate cycles C_new for the
decision. Break-even requires Fmax_new/Fmax_parent > C_new/C. The one-clock
registered-operand DSP path, its completion selection, unchanged JALR
forwarding and register-file reads can still limit Fmax or erase the gain.
Inspect all three routed seeds and verify one shared multiplier, successful
placement within the resource target, and preserved block RAM inference.
Report missing timing arcs as unavailable evidence, not zero delay.

During implementation run the unchanged lint, real/ALTOPS unit, formal
including liveness, stalled cosim and three-seed FPGA gates. Compare the
same binaries and bus schedules against the accepted parent, preserving
every existing correctness assertion; only multiply latency expectations
change to the proposed schedule. Require canonical 6 KB CRCs, validation
UART text, bounded accesses and the exact start/stop markers. The prior
logs identify a pre-existing 2 KB evaluator default: keep its reported
fitness distinct from the requested 6 KB measurement and do not modify
benchmark sources, evaluator settings, wrappers or constraints.

title: Bimodal prediction with branch comparison split across EX and MEM
motivation:
The current fetch path predicts sequentially and discards a useful slot
on each taken transfer. Predictor r13s2 reduced measured cycles by 5.02%
on the evaluator's 2 KB fixture and 4.91% on its separate 6 KB run, but
its 140.61 MHz median lost to the current 184.84 MHz implementation.
Every routed seed was limited by EX/MEM destination-tag forwarding
through branch comparison into recovery_pending.D. Registering the
completed recovery decision left the expensive forwarding-plus-full-
comparison chain intact. Earlier r10s2 also showed that merely balancing
a wholly combinational comparator was insufficient. The promising next
predictor experiment is to place a real register boundary INSIDE branch
validation, while preserving the two-slot repair schedule established
by r13s2 and its actual deferred writeback protocol.

on each taken transfer. Predictor r13s2 reduced measured cycles by 5.02%
on the evaluator's 2 KB fixture and 4.91% on its separate 6 KB run, but

through branch comparison into recovery_pending.D. Registering the
