hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one 64-entry bimodal direct-control predictor whose branch
validation is partitioned between EX and MEM. Keep the same prediction
policy as r13s2 so the principal experimental variable is the validation
boundary: EX registers independent byte-comparison summaries; MEM
combines those summaries and performs recovery. Do not register a full
branch predicate or full misprediction decision after forwarding in EX.
Ordinary instructions retain their existing execution/retirement stages.

Index 64 two-bit saturating counters with fetch PC[7:2], reset to 01.
Raw imem_data predecode admits only legal BRANCH funct3 0/1/4/5/6/7 and
direct JAL. A conditional predicts taken from the counter MSB; an
eligible direct JAL predicts taken unconditionally. Require aligned
source and target: with aligned PC, B immediate bit 1 is instr[8] and
J immediate bit 1 is instr[21]. Form exact sign-extended B/J immediates,
full-width modulo-2^32 targets, and an independent PC+4. Select prediction
data using raw predecode/counter state, independently of acceptance,
stalls, flush, and repair. Apply it only on actual fetch acceptance.
Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC register. JALR predicts PC+4;
there is no BTB, target truncation, RAS, or speculative history.

Carry the consumed predicted_taken and two-bit counter snapshot with
the accepted instruction through ID/EX and EX/MEM. ID also registers
whether the branch is signed relational. Metadata uses the ordinary
payload capture/hold domain; controls and valid alone determine whether
it has an owner. Preserve control-zero bubbles, full held metadata, the
existing fetch NOP mask, and separation of payload enables from flush.

In EX use the existing forwarded rs1 and rs2. For each of four independent
eight-bit slices j, compute E[j] = (rs1_byte == rs2_byte) and
L[j] = (rs1_byte < rs2_byte). Slices 0 through 2 compare unsigned. Slice 3
compares signed bytes for BLT/BGE and unsigned bytes otherwise; this
makes lexicographic combination produce the correct signed or unsigned
whole-word ordering. Equal summaries are identical for both modes.
Register these eight summary bits at the EX/MEM boundary with ordinary
payload capture. All four comparisons operate in parallel. No cross-
slice merge, branch-op selection, direction XOR, or repair qualification
may precede this register boundary. Do not replicate comparators over
every forwarding-source pair or alter ALU SLT/SLTU and M arithmetic.

EX independently registers full control-target and fall-through addresses
without consulting the branch outcome. Reuse existing EX/MEM fields:
raw branch_target can hold PC+B/J immediate or the bit-zero-cleared
forwarded JALR sum; raw pc_next can hold PC+4. Their payload enables must
not depend on outcome or recovery. Carry decoder controls and actual
post-forward operand values as before. EX must no longer compute a
separate full-width branch comparator for pc_next, alignment traps,
training, or redirect: those consumers all use the registered summaries.

Add a combinational MEM control resolver between the raw EX/MEM record
and its MEM/forwarding consumers. Merge summaries in two balanced levels:
merge (3,2) and (1,0), then merge those pairs. For high/low children use
E = E_high AND E_low and L = L_high OR (E_high AND L_low).
Select E for BEQ/BNE or L for relational branches and XOR branch_op[0]
to obtain the architectural predicate. Use that same predicate for the
actual branch_taken, taken-only target-alignment trap, resolved pc_next,
and predictor outcome. Resolve JAL/JALR from registered target/control
fields. Preserve sequential continuation and suppressed jump-link write
on target misalignment, and preserve decoder illegality.

The resolver emits a normalized architectural EX/MEM record; raw pc_next
is only its registered fall-through candidate, never RVFI's unresolved
answer. Feed normalized controls to forwarding as well as MEM. Qualify
jump reg_write using registered jump alignment alone: a branch already
has reg_write=0, so its comparison must not enter another instruction's
forwarding-write-enable cone. Memory controls remain unchanged and
independent of branch summaries. Keep the directly registered normal
EX/MEM memory-address bank separate from this resolver and result muxes.

Compute recovery in MEM from valid, legal registered control ownership
and the resolved decision. A direct transfer repairs when consumed
predicted_taken differs from its actual legal aligned transfer; every
legal aligned JALR repairs to its target. Conservatively repairing a
direction mismatch with displacement +4 is acceptable. Misaligned
transfers that were necessarily predicted sequentially trap and keep
PC+4. Illegal or ordinary instructions never own recovery. There is no
immediate EX redirect fallback and no additional recovery-event register
after the MEM merge. With summaries captured at E0, MEM repairs at E1:
correct predictions discard zero slots and errors discard two slots.

MEM recovery overrides imem backpressure and younger fetch prediction,
flushes ID/fetch, and kills the younger EX owner before EX/MEM capture.
Suppress its divider request, acceptance, effective div_wait, and all
predictor actions; emit zero EX/MEM controls and valid. A killed younger
divide cannot already have launched because it entered EX at E0. Do not
reset the divider or completion bank. Give older recovery precedence
over younger load-use/divider holds. Compute dmem stalls independently;
a recovering control owner has no memory request. When an older memory
operation stalls a branch in EX, retain its complete operands/metadata
and capture summaries only on actual advancement. Preserve held-WB
forwarding and once-only retirement under arbitrary bus stalls.

Retain r13s2's real deferred commit for a recovering branch or jump. At
repair edge E1, MEM/WB captures the entire resolved owner with valid clear
and sets commit_pending. At E2, retain that record, assert valid once,
and clear commit_pending; the discarded incoming MEM record is the
recovery bubble. Corrected fetching and execution continue. Regfile
writes, jump-link forwarding, and all RVFI fields must describe this
actual WB owner and valid schedule. Correct predictions and ordinary
instructions use normal commit. Reset cancels pending ownership.
A corrected divide launches E3, accepts E11, and reaches valid MEM/WB
at E12, ten clocks after its recovering predecessor. Check both adjacent
retirement gaps, including a DIV/REM predecessor. Preserve the existing
formal bound and eight-compute-clock divider; do not use RVFI-only delays
or fabricate retirement to work around the r6s2 liveness failure.

Train a surviving nontrapping conditional branch once on MEM advancement,
including an owner causing recovery. Saturate its saved counter snapshot
using the MEM predicate, then register train_pending, index, and value.
The following edge writes the table from those registered fields alone.
Lookup observes pre-edge contents, with no update-to-lookup bypass.
Held, invalid, and killed owners cannot train. The extra training delay
and aliased stale snapshots may reduce accuracy but cannot change the
architecturally certified target or bypass validation.

Forecast a 4 percent net fitness improvement with low confidence. Five
percent fewer cycles with one percent lower Fmax would yield about
4.21 percent higher fitness; the corresponding break-even frequency is
about 175.60 MHz against 184.84 MHz. These are conditional estimates.
Byte-comparator mapping, MEM-merge-to-squash depth, target addition, IF
target selection, training staleness, or deferred-commit fanout can erase
the benefit. Inspect every routed seed and mapped dependencies: EX
forwarding paths must terminate at local summary flops before a full
predicate is formed, while every repair input must originate in the
registered MEM owner. Merely moving the worst endpoint is not success.

During implementation run unchanged lint, unit, formal including liveness,
ISS cosim, CRC/UART/OOB, marker-window, resource and three-seed FPGA gates.
Measure exact iterations/cycle, correct predictions, both direction
errors, JALR repairs, table updates, and median routed Fmax on identical
ELFs for parent and candidate. Identify the actual working set: prior
evaluator logs describe a 2 KB fixture and separate 6 KB measurements.
Preserve the required 6 KB validation and report any fixture discrepancy
without changing benchmark or evaluator files. Keep nret=1, all ports,
strict decoding, true resolved RVFI PCs, monotonic order, arithmetic and
result-bank ownership, and all hard invariants. This proposal targets
only cores/bench RTL and its permitted cocotb tests.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the bimodal predictor with the branch comparison split inside EX/MEM. Correctness gates pass, but the forecast fitness improvement was not achieved: median routed Fmax is 158.20 MHz versus the reproduced parent's 184.84 MHz. The 2 KB fixture loses 9.8844% fitness despite 5.0247% fewer cycles; the separate required 6 KB run loses 9.9901% fitness despite 4.9132% fewer cycles.

The implementation follows the proposed ownership and timing protocol:

- `branch_predictor.sv` provides 64 two-bit counters indexed by fetch PC[7:2], reset to 01. `control_resolve.sv` registers the advancing branch's saved-snapshot update; the table writes those registered fields on the next edge. There is no update-to-lookup bypass.
- IF uses raw instruction bits for legal BRANCH/JAL eligibility, aligned source/target checks, exact sign-extended immediates, full-width target addition, and independent PC+4. Only actual acceptance applies prediction. JALR remains sequentially predicted. The PC register directly drives imem address, and the NOP mask remains intact.
- ID carries consumed direction/counter metadata and registers signed-relational mode in the ordinary payload domain. EX captures four independent byte equal/less pairs from its existing forwarded operands. For signed comparison, the top byte's sign bits are inverted before one unsigned eight-bit comparison; this is equivalent to signed byte ordering and avoids duplicate signed/unsigned comparators. There is no EX full-word branch predicate, direction inversion, alignment decision, or redirect.
- Raw EX/MEM `pc_next` contains PC+4 and `branch_target` contains the independently computed direct/JALR target. Raw `branch_taken` is zero. MEM merges (3,2) and (1,0), then merges the two pairs; it selects equality/ordering and applies branch-op inversion. Its normalized record supplies the actual predicate, taken-only alignment trap, architectural next PC, and forwarding/MEM controls. Jump write-enable qualification depends only on registered jump control and target alignment.
- MEM recovery overrides younger stalls/prediction, flushes ID/fetch, and kills EX controls/valid. Divider request, acceptance and effective wait are suppressed without resetting the divider or its completion bank. Payload capture remains independent of recovery, and the directly registered normal memory-address bank remains separate from result selection and resolution.
- A recovering owner is captured in the real MEM/WB bank with valid clear at E1. At E2 that entire bank is retained, valid asserts once, and `commit_pending` clears while the incoming recovery bubble is discarded. RVFI and register writes use this actual owner. Normal instructions and correct predictions retain ordinary commit timing. Reset cancels pending ownership.

No architectural deviation from the hypothesis was needed. The top-byte sign-bit transform is an equivalent implementation choice. Fetch masking and bus-stall equations were separated into explicit independent assignments to remove a false combinational-loop warning in cocotb's visibility-enabled Verilator build. A new optional profiling test binds a simulation-only observer to either revision; it does not change production RTL, ports, the cosim harness, or benchmark/evaluator files. `nret: 1`, strict decoding, ALU SLT/SLTU, multiplier/divider arithmetic, and the existing completion bank are unchanged.

Resources increased from 5,485 LUT4 / 2,119 DFF to 5,972 LUT4 / 2,301 DFF. All seeds fit and route. Final resynthesis after the fetch-mask cleanup has identical mapped cell names, types, parameters, port directions and connections to the routed netlist; only source-location attributes differ, so the reported routes apply to the final implementation.

Mapped dependency inspection found eight distinct summary flops: equality byte 0..3 maps to `cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_160`..`_157`, and less-than byte 0..3 maps to `_164`..`_161`. Each D cone contains only its local operand byte and forwarding/hold controls; the top less-than cone additionally contains the registered signed mode. No summary D cone contains another summary flop, a cross-byte merge, or a completed branch predicate. The recovery-decision cone feeding deferred-commit ownership contains registered EX/MEM validity, decoder control, consumed direction, target alignment and all eight summary outputs, plus reset; it has no current EX operand/forwarding source. Jump alignment, rather than branch comparison, qualifies forwarding writes. All normal memory-address bits remain directly flop-driven. The seed-2 forwarding path terminates at a local summary as intended, but the other two seeds expose a slower ordinary ALU path. Moving the comparison boundary therefore does not establish an overall timing win.

Using median routed Fmax times the exact measured ratios, 2 KB fitness changes from 411.534270 to 370.856580 iterations/s; 6 KB changes from 56.290724 to 50.667214 iterations/s. Break-even Fmax for these measured cycle counts is 175.552289 MHz for 2 KB and 175.758482 MHz for 6 KB. The implementation remains below both thresholds. Residual ordinary ALU delay, local forwarding-to-byte comparison delay and routing overhead erase the cycle benefit; this candidate should be classified as a measured fitness regression, not an accepted improvement.

title: Flatten jump-link override into the ALU result selector
motivation:
The accepted EX stage first selects an ALU result and then applies
in.ctrl.is_jump ? PC+4 : alu_result before the normal EX/MEM register.
Every ordinary result passes through this second selection. The saved
accepted-core reports from r14s0 identify ID/EX alu_op[3] to normal
EX/MEM result[23] as critical in seeds 1 and 3; seed 2 is limited by
forwarding/JALR. Flattening the serial result selections is a focused
opportunity to improve the first path without changing instruction
latency or operand routing.

The micro_opt history cautions against broad ALU restructuring: r2s0's
registered one-hot masks changed one MULT36X36 into three and regressed
fitness 5.98%; r14s0's shared right shifter deepened an operation-control
cone and regressed 4.35%. Both retained the external jump-result mux.
This proposal tests only that remaining selection boundary, preserving
the existing arithmetic expressions and encoded operation values.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Express jump-link and ordinary ALU selection as one mutually exclusive
combinational case in alu.sv. Add internal inputs link_select and
link_data[31:0], driven by the existing ID/EX is_jump and the existing
EX PC+4 expression. Replace case(op) with casez({link_select, op}):
the six-bit pattern 1????? selects link_data, and each existing ALU arm
uses the exact six-bit key {1'b0, ALU_<operation>}. Retain a defined-zero
default. Wildcards occur only in the jump arm's five operation bits;
do not use casex, undefined result bits, or synthesis assumptions.
In ex_stage.sv capture alu_result directly into reg_q.alu_result,
removing the separate post-ALU jump mux rather than moving that mux
unchanged into the ALU module.

The combined function must equal the old expression for every defined
link_select, all 32 operation encodings, and arbitrary operands and
link_data. In particular, link_select must override the normal output
even for DIV/REM or unsupported internal operation codes. Pass the raw
registered is_jump bit, without valid, trap, stall or completion
qualification. This preserves inactive normal-bank captures and the
existing synthetic jump-plus-DIV ownership tests as well as all actual
decoded instructions. The divider continues receiving its original
encoded op and operands; link selection neither starts nor cancels it.

Keep the arithmetic expressions, all three multiplier expressions,
individual multiplication case arms, real/ALTOPS formulas, shifters,
forwarding muxes and ALU operand muxes unchanged. Add no predecode
registers, one-hot mask/OR networks, operation re-encoding, result
banks, instruction bubbles or stage boundaries. Preserve the existing
PC+4 arithmetic and branch/JALR target and alignment logic. Only the
two serial result selections are being flattened.

Keep synchronous reset, payload capture independent of bubble and
completion controls, dmem holds, load interlocks, eight-compute-clock
divide acceptance, held responses and divide-bank ownership intact.
The direct normal EX/MEM bank must still drive mem_addr; do not route
the post-register divide-bank mux into the memory-address interface.
Instruction legality, misalignment traps, raw RVFI source values,
retirement order, bus effects and the nret=1 top-level ports stay
equivalent, including suppressed link writes on trapped jumps.

Predict an unmeasured 3% fitness improvement through Fmax alone, with
identical marker-window cycles for identical binaries and bus-stall
schedules. A flat case gives synthesis the opportunity to merge the
link term into parallel result selection; it does not establish that
a mapped mux level will disappear. Shared decode fanout, disrupted
DSP sharing, placement or the unchanged forwarding/JALR path may
erase the benefit. Inspect pre-mapping mux structure, mapped normal
result cones and all three routed critical paths. Check preservation
of the accepted one-MULT36X36 and four-DPX9B mapping. Do not infer
timing margin from missing arcs or from source-level mux counts.

During implementation run unchanged lint, unit tests, formal including
liveness and unique retirement, and real-arithmetic ISS cosimulation.
Compare full valid RVFI records, retirement cycles and accepted memory
effects against the accepted core on directed mixed programs with
both buses stalled. Evaluate median Fmax over the unchanged three
seeds and exact marker-bracketed CoreMark iteration/cycle ratios.
Require the canonical 6 KB CRCs, validation UART literal and bounded
accesses. Prior implementation notes identify a pre-existing 2 KB
evaluator default; if it persists, report its fitness separately
from the requested 6 KB measurement without changing any contract
file, benchmark source, wrapper, evaluator or other core.

title: Separate load/store address generation from the general EX result bank
motivation:
The accepted core exposes a separate mem_addr port, but its driver is
still reg_q.alu_result: the same EX/MEM register that captures the full
normal ALU selection and the JAL/JALR link-value mux. Consequently,
general execution results and load/store addresses share a register
boundary and its fanout even though memory instructions need only
forwarded rs1 plus their immediate. The current parent reaches
184.84 MHz with 5485 LUT4s, leaving resource headroom for a dedicated
address-generation lane without another execution cycle.

Relevant structural experiments support testing this precise boundary,
without establishing that it will improve timing. r2s1 showed that a
post-register result mux on the memory address destroys BRAM address
absorption. r5s1 gained 7.14% by separating wide payload capture from
unrelated control. r7s1's multiply output bank and r12s1's unified WB
bank instead regressed 6.73% and 14.04%; neither separated effective
address computation from general ALU-result capture. This proposal
keeps a direct registered address and the existing result-forwarding
topology while removing the general result selector from the address
register's input.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give load/store effective-address generation its own EX/MEM register
bank. This is the sole structural change: split the address datapath
from the architectural-result datapath at the existing stage boundary.
Preserve instruction issue, retirement and all execution latencies.

In ex_stage.sv, compute address_sum = rs1 + in.imm directly from the
existing fully forwarded raw rs1 and the ID/EX immediate. Add one
32-bit address_q register, synchronously cleared on reset and captured
on every !stall edge. Drive the existing mem_addr output directly from
address_q. Keep all 32 address bits, including the low byte-position
bits used by alignment checks and lane masks. Legal LOAD and STORE
decoding already guarantees that this sum equals their existing ALU
address. Do not select address_sum using alu_op, alu_src, is_jump,
memory validity, divider status, or the normal ALU's output.

Leave reg_q.alu_result, its existing ALU and link selection, the divider
completion bank, div_result_sel_q, out.alu_result, and both ordinary
forwarding paths unchanged. In particular, add no new result-bank mux
to EX forwarding or WB. The new address register replaces the present
mem_addr alias; it does not replace the normal architectural-result
register or sit after it. core.sv and mem_stage.sv already carry this
independent address connection, so their interfaces and behavior need
no redesign. No core_pkg bundle change is needed.

Match the existing payload ownership exactly. A dmem stall holds
address_q and the complete EX/MEM owner together, preserving every
outstanding request's address, data and byte mask until acceptance.
Bubbles, redirects and divider computation may update the unowned
address payload on an unstalled edge, but must retain the current
zero-control/invalid discipline so these values cannot issue a request.
Divider acceptance cannot select its result onto mem_addr. Reset must
clear the address bank even during a hold. Do not add a memory-op
write enable or flush/completion mux to this bank: that would put
unrelated ownership control back into the intended simple datapath.

The intended timing benefit is to give memory-address capture a fixed
forwarding-plus-add cone and separate its physical load from general
result capture. Keep the existing shared multiplier and divider, ALU
operation encoding, hazard policy, branch resolution, RF and WB intact.
Do not introduce a cache, speculative memory transaction, extra stage,
memory forwarding path, opcode-specific shortcut, or benchmark-specific
address assumption. Preserve nret=1, every legality and trap rule,
alignment handling, x0 semantics, raw RVFI operands, consecutive
retirement order, and the real and ALTOPS arithmetic schedules.

Forecast a low-confidence 3% fitness gain from Fmax alone. For identical
binaries and bus schedules, marker-window cycles should be unchanged.
This is an unmeasured forecast: the extra adder and register may worsen
placement or increase forwarded-rs1 fanout, and the unchanged normal
result-selection, register-read and JALR paths may still limit Fmax.
Break-even requires median Fmax to improve if cycles are unchanged;
otherwise use the actual Fmax ratio divided by the actual cycle ratio.

Inspect the synthesized driver of each memory-address bit to establish
that it comes directly from the new bank, with no general-result or
divider-bank mux after that register. Check that its input is the
fixed effective-address sum, not a recreated general ALU selection.
Require preserved FPGA memory inference, including the parent's four
DPX9B cells rather than RAM16SDP4 expansion, and no replicated multiplier.
Measure all three routed seeds and inspect both the new address cone
and the unchanged result/forwarding cones. Treat missing timing arcs
as unavailable evidence, not demonstrated margin. Keep placement
within the resource target and use the median Fmax for fitness.

During implementation run the unchanged lint, unit, formal including
liveness, and stalled ISS-cosim gates. Compare retirement timing, all
contract-checked RVFI fields and accepted memory transactions against
the accepted parent. Memory data with zero masks and the idle bus
address retain the existing contract's interpretation; do not change
the checker or force equality by reconnecting the old result bank.
Require exact addresses and data whenever a request or RVFI mask is
active, including misalignment suppression and MMIO marker ordering.
Preserve every existing correctness assertion; adapt bank-alias unit
expectations to check the now-independent banks explicitly.

Use identical binaries and stall seeds for parent/candidate CoreMark
measurements, validating the requested 6 KB CRCs, validation UART
literal, bounded accesses and start/stop markers. Prior logs identify
a pre-existing 2 KB evaluator default: retain its unchanged reported
score separately from the requested 6 KB result. Do not modify any
benchmark source, evaluator, wrapper, constraint or other core.

title: Bimodal prediction with operand-registered MEM validation
motivation:
The bench winner predicts sequentially and discards a fetch/decode slot
on each taken transfer. Predictor r13s2 reduced 2 KB marker cycles by
5.0247% and required 6 KB cycles by 4.9132%, but forwarding followed by
full comparison into recovery_pending limited median Fmax to 140.61 MHz.
r14s2 kept that prediction policy and repair schedule, registering byte
summaries instead. It reached 158.20 MHz, still below the approximately
175.76 MHz break-even point for its measured 6 KB saving. Its seed-2
limiting path still crossed forwarding and byte equality; the other
seeds were limited by ordinary ALU selection. Partial comparison before
the register therefore did not establish a sufficient timing cut.

The existing EX/MEM bundle already captures the exact forwarded rs1_val
and rs2_val for RVFI, with independent payload enables. Use those
registers as the entire operand boundary for predictor validation.
This differs from r6s2, which registered an already resolved next PC,
r13s2's completed recovery predicate, and r14s2's EX byte summaries.
It removes predictor comparison logic from EX instead of adding more
summary or event flops to the end of its forwarding path. Routed timing
elsewhere remains a material risk; no Fmax improvement is assumed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one 64-entry bimodal direct-control predictor with all branch
comparison and validation after the existing EX/MEM operand registers.
Keep r14s2's prediction policy and two-slot repair schedule so the main
experimental variable is the placement of the comparison boundary.
Ordinary execution stages, arithmetic resources, and memory timing
remain unchanged. This is a predictor experiment, not an ALU redesign.

Index 64 two-bit saturating counters with fetch PC[7:2], reset to 01.
Raw imem_data predecode admits only BRANCH opcode 0x63 with funct3
0/1/4/5/6/7 and direct JAL opcode 0x6f. Conditional direction is the
counter MSB; eligible JAL predicts taken unconditionally. Require an
aligned source and target for taken prediction: with aligned PC,
B-immediate bit 1 is instr[8] and J-immediate bit 1 is instr[21]. Form
exact sign-extended B/J immediates and full 32-bit modulo targets, with
independent PC+4. Raw predecode/counter outputs select prediction data;
acceptance, stalls, flush, and repair only govern capture or recovery.
Keep imem_addr directly driven by the PC register and preserve the
current fetch NOP mask. Apply a prediction only on actual fetch
acceptance. JALR predicts sequentially. Add no BTB or return stack.

Carry consumed predicted_taken and the two-bit counter snapshot with
the accepted instruction through ID/EX and EX/MEM. ID also registers
signed_relational for BLT/BGE. Metadata belongs to ordinary payload
capture/hold; invalid metadata is inert. Preserve control-zero bubbles
and full metadata retention during load-use, memory, and divider holds.
A table update cannot retroactively change a consumed prediction.

EX retains normal operand forwarding and captures its exact rs1/rs2
values into the existing EX/MEM rs1_val/rs2_val fields. Branches use
these ordinary values; completed divides retain their existing operand
snapshots. Do not compute even byte/nibble equality, less-than, a
branch predicate, or prediction error before these operand registers.
Remove EX branch comparison from every control-transfer consumer,
including pc_next, alignment trapping, training, and redirect. Keep
ALU SLT/SLTU unchanged because they are arithmetic instructions.

EX independently captures the full direct/JALR target and PC+4 in
existing EX/MEM payload fields, without consulting branch outcome.
Raw branch_target holds PC+imm or the forwarded JALR sum with bit 0
cleared; raw pc_next holds PC+4. Raw branch_taken is inactive. Preserve
PC+4 link results, the divider completion bank, and the separate direct
registered normal memory-address bank. No outcome-controlled payload
enable, additional branch operand bank, or recovery-event flop is
required at EX/MEM. Decoder controls pass to MEM for final resolution.

Add a combinational MEM control resolver using ONLY the registered
EX/MEM owner. Compute equality and ordering from rs1_val/rs2_val there.
Use eight parallel four-bit E/L comparisons followed by three explicit
balanced merge levels: E = E_high AND E_low, and
L = L_high OR (E_high AND L_low). For the top nibble, invert both sign
bits when registered signed_relational is set; lower nibbles are
unsigned. This gives signed or unsigned 32-bit ordering without a
whole-word serial subtract. All nibble computation and merging occur
AFTER the operand registers, with no additional pipeline stage.
Select equality for BEQ/BNE and less-than for relational branches;
branch_op[0] inverts the selected relation. Share this one predicate
among architectural branch_taken, taken-only alignment trapping,
actual pc_next, prediction validation, and training.

Emit a normalized architectural EX/MEM record for MEM/WB and forwarding.
Its pc_next is the resolved target or PC+4, never the raw candidate.
Resolve JAL/JALR and target alignment from registered target/control
fields. Preserve decoder illegality, sequential trap continuation and
suppression of misaligned jump link writes. Qualify jump reg_write
only with registered jump legality/alignment; branches already have
reg_write=0, so branch comparison must not enter the younger EX
forwarding-write-enable cone. Memory control is independent of this
resolver's predicate, and its address bypasses the resolver entirely.

For a valid legal direct branch/JAL, repair when consumed direction
differs from the actual aligned transfer decision. Every legal aligned
JALR repairs to its registered target. Direction mismatch at displacement
+4 may conservatively repair. Ordinary or illegal instructions cannot
predict taken or own repair. Misaligned transfers were predicted
sequentially and trap with sequential continuation. There is no live
EX redirect fallback and no event register after MEM comparison.
With operands captured at E0, a miss repairs at E1; correct predictions
discard zero younger slots, errors discard two under zero wait.

MEM repair overrides imem backpressure and younger predictions/holds,
flushes fetch and ID, and kills the younger EX owner before EX/MEM
capture. Clear that owner's entire controls and valid; suppress its
divider launch, acceptance, effective div_wait, and predictor actions.
A killed younger divide has just entered EX and cannot already have
launched. Do not reset the divider or its result bank on repair. Keep
memory backpressure independent: the repairing control owner has no
memory transaction. An older memory hold freezes a branch in EX and
its metadata until real advancement; preserve retained-WB forwarding.

Use the real deferred-commit schedule already validated in r11s2,
r13s2, and r14s2. At repair edge E1, MEM/WB captures the complete
normalized repairing owner with valid clear and sets commit_pending.
At E2 retain that record, assert valid once, and clear commit_pending;
the discarded incoming MEM entry is the recovery bubble. Corrected
fetch/execution continue. Actual regfile writeback and every RVFI field
identify this same owner and valid cycle; jump links remain available
through the existing forwarding paths. Ordinary instructions and
correctly predicted transfers commit normally. Reset cancels pending
ownership. This is an actual one-clock WB postponement, not an RVFI-only
delay. With zero wait, a corrected divide launches E3, accepts E11,
and reaches valid MEM/WB E12, ten clocks after its recovering owner.
Check both neighboring retirement gaps, including DIV/REM predecessors;
preserve the formal liveness bound and eight-compute-clock divider.

Train a surviving nontrapping conditional branch exactly once on MEM
advancement, including the repairing owner. Saturate its saved counter
snapshot using the resolved predicate and register train_pending,
source index, and final value. The next edge writes from those
registered fields alone. Use pre-edge lookup contents without a write
bypass. Holds, invalid entries, and squashed successors cannot train.
Delayed or aliased snapshots can reduce accuracy but cannot affect
architectural correctness. Keep this schedule identical to r14s2.

Forecast a 3% net fitness improvement with low confidence. Reproducing
r14s2's 6 KB cycle ratio would require approximately 181.03 MHz for
that gain, or 175.76 MHz merely to break even against 184.84 MHz.
These are conditional targets, not measured results. MEM comparator
depth plus squash fanout can become critical; fetch target arithmetic,
ordinary ALU selection, routing and commit fanout can still dominate.
Inspect all three routed seeds and mapped register boundaries. No
branch comparison may precede the EX/MEM operand registers, and no
current EX operand/forwarding source may enter the MEM recovery cone.
Do not infer success merely because a critical endpoint has moved.

During implementation run unchanged lint, unit, formal/liveness, ISS
cosim, CRC/UART/OOB, marker-window, resource and three-seed FPGA gates.
Compare identical ELFs and stall settings for parent/candidate. Record
exact iterations/cycle, both direction-error counts, correct predictions,
JALR repairs, table updates and median Fmax. Prior logs distinguish the
evaluator's 2 KB fixture from separate required 6 KB runs; identify the
actual working set and preserve both the unchanged evaluator and the
required 6 KB CRC/validation checks without changing contract files.
Keep nret=1, exact external IO, strict decoding, real resolved RVFI PCs,
monotonic retirement and all arithmetic and ownership invariants.
Implementation scope is only bench RTL and its permitted cocotb tests.

implementation_notes:
# Bimodal prediction with operand-registered MEM validation

Implemented on bench RTL only, with permitted bench tests. Parent HEAD:
`796ebe05b7a7fd59bf575595aa786aa676e7581c`.

The architectural hypothesis is implemented and passes local correctness gates.
The measured fitness forecast did **not** succeed: the required 6 KB marker
window is 4.913177709% shorter, but median Fmax is 160.88 MHz versus the
reproduced parent median of 184.84 MHz. Required 6 KB fitness falls 8.465299726%.

## Implementation

- Added a 64-entry two-bit direction table indexed by fetch PC[7:2], reset to
  `01`. Registered training transactions write on the following edge; fetch
  consumes pre-edge table contents without bypass. Training saturates the
  instruction's saved counter snapshot, including aliased/stale snapshots.
- Fetch uses raw legal BRANCH/JAL predecode, exact sign-extended full-width
  targets, independent PC+4, source/target alignment qualification, and
  accepted-only prediction application. JALR stays sequential. The PC register
  directly drives imem addressing and the original fetch NOP mask is retained.
- Added consumed direction, counter snapshot, and ID-decoded signed-relational
  payload metadata. Full memory/divider holds retain metadata; load-use and
  repair bubbles clear complete controls and validity independently of payload.
- Removed every branch comparator, branch predicate, control-transfer trap,
  and redirect from EX. Existing forwarded rs1/rs2 registers are the complete
  comparison boundary. Raw EX/MEM pc_next is PC+4, branch_taken is zero, and
  branch_target captures PC+imm or the forwarded JALR sum with bit 0 cleared.
  Link results, arithmetic resources, divider snapshots/completion bank, and
  the direct normal memory-address bank retain their existing structure.
- Added a MEM resolver with eight parallel nibble E/L comparisons and explicit
  8-to-4-to-2-to-1 balanced merges. Signed relational operations invert the two
  registered sign bits in the top nibble. One predicate drives branch outcome,
  taken-only target traps, normalized actual next PC, direction validation,
  and training. Jump forwarding write qualification depends only on registered
  jump control/legality/alignment, never branch operands or comparison.
- MEM repair directly redirects fetch, flushes ID, and clears all controls and
  valid of younger EX. It suppresses younger divide launch, acceptance, and
  effective wait without resetting the divider or its result bank. Independent
  memory backpressure still holds the complete older owner and retained WB data.
- Repair edge E1 captures the complete normalized MEM/WB owner with valid zero
  and sets commit_pending. E2 retains every field, asserts valid once, and
  clears pending ownership while discarding the incoming recovery bubble.
  Regfile writeback uses this same delayed owner/valid as RVFI. No EX recovery
  event register, extra operand bank, or comparison pipeline stage was added.
- Hazard outputs use independent continuous equations to expose their actual
  dependencies even to Verilator's public-signal instrumentation.

There is no ALU redesign, BTB, return stack, contract change, or nret change.
`alu.sv`, `div_unit.sv`, the decoder, and all evaluator/formal/FPGA/ISS contract
files are unchanged. The single retirement remains on the actual MEM/WB valid
signal and the original channel-0 port set.

## Local validation

- Required literal Verilator lint command: PASS, zero warnings. Final
  `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Unchanged `formal/run_all.sh`, with `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl`,
  `CORE_NAME=bench`, `JOBS=6`: **53 passed, 0 failed**. The script selected
  the unchanged single-issue wrapper/checks automatically. Both initial and
  final hardware checks passed, including liveness, unique, illegal, PC, and
  register checks. Formal RTL fix attempts: **0**. This is the standard
  ALTOPS gate; real arithmetic was additionally exercised by unit tests and ISS.
- Complete cocotb suite: **12 runners passed**, with the optional CoreMark
  instrumentation runner skipped in the ordinary unit invocation and run
  successfully separately. This includes 34 real and 34 ALTOPS ALU cases,
  six EX bank/kill cases in each arithmetic mode, 27 pipeline tests, all
  unchanged decoder/immediate/regfile checks, and new predictor/resolver/ID
  metadata checks. Pipeline tests use the unchanged Python ISS comparison and
  independently compare every accepted memory request under random and long
  stalls. The final focused pipeline rerun also passes.
- Directed checks cover both prediction errors, warm correct predictions,
  aliased branch snapshots, fetch/write edge collisions, complete deferred-WB
  data retention, reset of pending ownership, killed stores/divides, consecutive
  controls/links, strict illegality and target traps, every comparison nibble
  and merge level, forwarding, and metadata retention. All sixteen combinations
  of DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU predecessor and corrected successor check adjacent
  retirement gaps: two clocks into the recovering owner, ten clocks to the
  corrected divide, then one clock to its ordinary consumer. Divider acceptance
  remains eight compute clocks after launch; consecutive divides stay nine apart.
- Unchanged `tools.eval.cosim`: **passed, 2 ELFs** (selftest full ISS trace and
  evaluator CoreMark CRC/UART check).
- Unchanged synthesis, nextpnr script/constraints, and `tools.eval.fpga`:
  all three candidate seeds route successfully. Parent was also synthesized
  and routed with those identical scripts and all three seeds.
- Both parent and candidate separately pass the required 6 KB CRCs
  `crclist=d4b0`, `crcmatrix=be52`, `crcstate=5e47`, plus `seedcrc=8a02`,
  `crcfinal=5949`, ITERATIONS=10, the literal `Correct operation validated.`,
  EBREAK completion, OOB=false, and both timing markers.

All generated builds, staged unmodified contracts, and logs are under
`$TMPDIR/r15s2-validation`; the original shared formal tree was not written.
The existing Conda Python environment supplied cocotb/SBY dependencies.
The first unit run exposed old EX-redirect handles and old one-clock retirement
expectations for repairing consumers. Tests were updated to assert the specified
raw EX payload and exact real deferred-WB schedule; ISS checks and the ten-clock
liveness bound were retained. No formal counterexample occurred.

## Identical-ELF measurements

Both versions used the unchanged harness with
`50000000 --bench --istall --dstall`, default LFSR seed `0xDEADBEEF`,
ITERATIONS=10, and actual compiler option `-O3`. Parent RTL was extracted from
HEAD into scratch. Each ELF was built once and reused byte-for-byte across
parent and candidate. Only stop-marker minus start-marker cycles are counted.

The unchanged evaluator uses **TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=2000**, while the separately
required run uses **TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=6000**. CoreMark's printed Size is the
per-algorithm partition (666 and 2000 respectively), not the total working set.
Its unchanged static UART compiler string says `-O2`; the captured compiler

## Predictor events

The optional permitted test builds an observing subclass of the Verilator
model and includes the unchanged `test/cosim/main.cpp` verbatim. It samples
existing pre-edge internal signals and adds counts only to stderr. Its complete

contract binary byte-for-byte for both ELFs. No counters were added to RTL.

Direction errors below mean consumed sequential/actual taken and consumed
taken/actual sequential, respectively. Correct predictions count surviving legal
direct controls; JALR repairs are separate. Table updates count actual delayed

## Routed timing, boundaries, and fitness

| Implementation | Seed 1 MHz | Seed 2 MHz | Seed 3 MHz | Median MHz | LUT4 | FF | BSRAM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Parent | 190.33 | 184.84 | 168.69 | 184.84 | 5,485 | 2,119 | 4 |
| Candidate | 147.82 | 160.88 | 164.07 | 160.88 | 5,943 | 2,266 | 4 |

All three candidate critical paths start at
`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_166.Q`, mapped to ID/EX ctrl.alu_op[3]. They traverse
ordinary ALU selection/arithmetic. Seed 1 and seed 3 end at
`cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_44.D`, normal address/result bank bit 19; seed 2 ends at
`cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_57.D`, normal bank bit 6. Reported logic/routing delays
are 2.89/3.88 ns, 3.05/3.17 ns, and 2.89/3.21 ns respectively. The direct
address bank remains connected to the memory wrapper; BSRAM usage is unchanged.

Generic optimized and Gowin-mapped connectivity audits passed assertions:

- All 64 branch operand bits at the resolver input are existing register Qs;
  in the mapped design all are DFFR outputs. No comparison precedes them.
- The generic repair cone terminates in 77 EX/MEM register outputs, reset,
  and the independent MEM advancement control from io_dmemReady. It reaches
  no current EX operand/forwarding source. A control owner has no memory
  transaction, so this advancement qualification cannot delay its repair.
- The mapped deferred-commit D cone contains 75 registered source bits, all
  from EX/MEM, plus reset. Its reset cone additionally contains only pending
  ownership. No current EX/ID or divider arithmetic register enters recovery.
- Forwarding write-enable uses five registered control/alignment bits and
  no branch operand/comparison. The memory address directly aliases the
  normal EX/MEM result register; it bypasses control resolution and the
  divide-bank result selection.

Measured 2 KB fitness is 377.139106381 iter/s versus parent 411.534269846 iter/s
(-8.357788400%). Required 6 KB fitness is 51.525545932 iter/s versus parent
56.290724477 iter/s (-8.465299726%). The measured 6 KB cycle ratio requires
175.758482322 MHz to break even against the parent, which this candidate does
not reach. Operand registration established the intended comparison boundary,
but routed ordinary execution timing still prevents the forecast gain.

Primary evidence under `$TMPDIR/r15s2-validation`:
`formal-final.log`, `unit-complete.log`, `pipeline-final.log`, `cosim.json`,
`fpga.json`, `comparison.json`, `parent-fmax.json`, `bench-build.log`,
`boundary-audit.json`, `cores/bench/generated/pnr_seed{1,2,3}/nextpnr.log`, and
`parent/generated/pnr_seed{1,2,3}/nextpnr.log`. Instrumentation evidence is
`$TMPDIR/r15s2-predictor-metrics/metrics.json`; its pytest invocation passed.

The requested root implementation_notes.md is the only non-RTL/test source
artifact created in the worktree. No contract, other core, or helper script
outside the permitted source surface was edited.
lesson: - 2026-09-06 hyp-20260906-003-r15s2 (regression, -8.36%): Moving branch comparison entirely behind existing EX/MEM rs1_val/rs2_val registers isolated MEM recovery from live forwarding, but ordinary alu_op[3]-to-normal-result paths limited all three routed seeds to a 160.88 MHz median, below the 175.76 MHz needed to break even with the bimodal predictor's 4.91% reduction in 6 KB CoreMark cycles.
